# dilla-web-2b — say more: edits, deletes, reactions, replies, pins, mentions, images and files, end to end Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Let a person say more than a line of text. After this plan: (C) a message can be edited in place, deleted for everyone (the type-2 envelope, the delivery service's copy and every attachment reference it carried), reacted to with a fixed set of 32 emoji (one reaction per person per emoji), replied to (a quoted reference line that jumps to the original), pinned and unpinned (a pins list per conversation), and can mention people, `@everyone`, `@here` and roles in the readable syntax `<@…>` through an `@` autocomplete in the composer; the browser core folds envelope types 1–6 onto their targets in its apply unit (edits by group `seq`, reactions per user, pins from any member, folds whose target is not held kept until it arrives), the store moves from schema v2 to v3 by a real migration, and `protocol/04` says all of it. (D) an image or a file can be attached (button, drop or paste; at most 4 per message, 25 MiB each in a browser), is sealed in the core worker with WebCrypto AES-256-GCM under the `protocol/04` attachment AEAD this plan writes down with vectors first, uploaded as octet-stream under the per-user upload meter, confirmed only when its message is sent (unconfirmed uploads expire after `blobs.pending_ttl`), shown as a WebP thumbnail card or a file card, opened in a lightbox or saved, and deleted from the instance with its message; the served CSP admits `img-src 'self' blob:`. web-2c (leaf validation and safety numbers, search, the settings surface, diagnostics, the tab hand-over, typing) and web-3 (voice) follow and are out of this plan.

**Architecture:** Unchanged from web-1 and web-2a (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-05-dilla-web-1.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-dilla-web-2a.md`): one dedicated worker per tab owns the KEK, the encrypted OPFS store, the Rust core, the session token and the single gateway; Rust decides and persists, TypeScript transports, the page renders slices and sends commands. This plan adds to Rust the protocol/04 changes (the attachment element's `name`, `reply_to` required on types 1–6), the attachment AEAD primitives (used by the vectors and the native peer; the browser seals with WebCrypto), schema v3 with derived fold tables recomputed per target from the stored rows (`refold`), a timeline view that carries the folded body, the reply reference, reactions, the pin flag and attachment summaries and returns only displayable rows, a generalised `send_prepare` taking a CBOR request (type, `reply_to`, body, attachment descriptors) with the author rules, the purge record a delete leaves for its sender, own role ids for role mentions; to the facade ABI 6; to dillad the delete's membership check, pending blob references with a confirm route and their sweep, and the CSP row; to the native peer typed envelopes, deletes and attachments; to client-core the octet-stream path and an `upload` pacing bucket, the blob and delete route helpers, the attachment pipeline (WebCrypto seal and open checked against the vectors, worker thumbnails, the tray), mention helpers, and the worker's commands and slices for edits, deletes, reactions, pins, replies and attachments; to `@dilla/ui` the message toolbar, the reaction bar and emoji grid, the inline editor, the reply chip, the mention list, the pins dialog, the attachment tray, card, lightbox and drop overlay; to the page the conversation that composes them and mints `blob:` URLs from Blobs the worker transfers. Every new refusal states who can trigger it against an honest party (lesson e), every server behaviour a client relies on is added to `ModelDs`/`FakeServer` and, where the e2e drives it, to the native testkit peer (lesson f), and an attachment key never leaves the worker.

**Tech Stack:** As web-2a's: Rust 1.98.1, `dilla-core` on OpenMLS 0.9.0, `rusqlite` 0.40.2 (native SQLCipher; wasm `sqlite-wasm-rs` 0.5.5 with `sqlite3mc`, `sqlite-wasm-vfs` 0.2.0), `aes-gcm` 0.10.3, `sha2` (as locked), `hkdf` 0.13, `ed25519-dalek` 2.2, `zeroize` 1, wasm-bindgen 0.2.128 / wasm-pack 0.15.0 under `wasm-release`; Go 1.27.0 (`github.com/jonasthim/dilla`), sqlc v1.31.1, goose migrations; TypeScript 5.9.3, React 19.3.0, Vite 7, vitest 3, Storybook 9, ESLint 9.39.5 with typescript-eslint 8.71.1, jsx-a11y 6.10.2, react-hooks 7.1.1; WebCrypto (`crypto.subtle` AES-GCM, SHA-256) and `OffscreenCanvas`/`createImageBitmap` in the worker; Playwright 1.63.0 exact (Chromium 153 under `channel: 'chromium'`, Firefox 155, WebKit 26.6 in CI only); the Rust `dilla-testkit web-driver` as the native counterparty. No new dependency of any kind (pin table below).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-dilla-design.md` (E2EE channels L216–217 "no remote loads; only sender-attached previews and re-hosted encrypted attachments", the design section L166–330 with the message row, toolbar and composer L270–272, Clients L510–524 with L512 "attachment upload/download with client-generated thumbnails (canvas) and per-blob random AES-256-GCM keys", Data model L590–594, Error handling L600–637, Testing L637–653), `docs/design/brief.md` (the visual authority; brief:123–126 the feed, grouped messages, the pill composer with attach; brief:66 and :80 the `--mention` token and `--r-pill` for reactions; brief:141–152 what the chrome never shows, incl. "the drop-overlay copy about encryption"; brief:186 the reply-reference flash of 1.4 s), the Mesh handoff `docs/design/reference/mesh-handoff/README.md:100–115` (upload tray, mention popup, reply chip, hover toolbar React · Reply · Edit · Delete, reactions, reply reference, "edited") and `chat-app.jsx:388–393` (the 32-emoji grid), and the normative `protocol/01-groups.md`, `02-delivery-service.md`, `04-envelope-and-franking.md`, `09-http-api.md`, each amended by the tasks named in "Protocol and spec edits in this plan" with a `07-versioning.md` row. Authorities in order: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-06-dilla-web-2/facts/rulings.md` (the three plans; Q15–Q21 bind this plan; Q01–Q14 provisional), `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-05-dilla-web/facts/rulings.md` (C1–C24, F1–F18 still bind), the web-2a plan's Global Constraints, Interface ledger and Follow-up cards, the web-2a ledger `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-06-dilla-web-2a/progress.md`, the web-1 plan; then `facts/interfaces.md` and `facts/deviations.md` of the web-2 research, the critic, the gap files G1–G8 and the lens files (`facts-messages.md`, `facts-attachments.md`, `facts-core-engine.md` above all); then the spec and the code. Where a facts file and the code disagree, **the code wins** and the task says so; this head records every such case it met in "Rulings made by the architect".

**Never written:** everything web-1 and web-2a forbid (web-2a Global Constraints "Never written", as amended for the recovery key crossing twice on a two-factor sign-in) — Go MLS code; cgo; an ORM; a router library; a `dillad serve` flag or config key that exists for tests; CORS or `OPTIONS`; COOP/COEP; a gateway `resume` frame; `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`; a second `DillaStorage` or a long-lived `ConnHandle` clone; MLS, TLS or credential parsing in TypeScript; a key, token, KEK, recovery key, enrolment assertion or host password in `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, a cookie, a URL, a log line, a slice or a `postMessage` to anything but the owning page; `innerHTML`/`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; inline `<script>`/`<style>`; `eval`; a `data:` or `blob:` worker; any new runtime dependency. Added by this plan: **an attachment's `key`, `nonce` or plaintext descriptor in any slice, any command result other than the decrypted `Blob` of `openAttachment`, any log line, or any store other than the envelope the core already keeps** (the tray's descriptors live in worker memory only; `attachment_get` reads them back from the stored envelope on demand); a decrypted attachment cache of any kind (Q17: no OPFS file, no IndexedDB record, no core table holds attachment plaintext); a `blob:` URL minted in the worker (G5: it dies with the worker; the page mints them from transferred Blobs and revokes them on unmount); a `data:` URL for an image; `connect-src blob:`; any `media-src` change (web-3); a `Notification` icon (the CSP widening is for attachment images only); the attachment AEAD in the browser through the wasm core (Q16: WebCrypto in the worker); an image decoder, resizer or emoji library; rendering a message body as HTML or markdown (text children and mention pills only); an edit, delete, reaction or pin applied to the page's state before the core folded it (the pending action shows as an indicator, never as the result); a server-side record that ties a blob to a message (the instance learns references and sizes, as today: `protocol/08:74`); a change to `core/dilla-core-wasi` or the wasi ABI; `protocol/08` edits (web-2c).

**Copy rules (F10) and the lint that enforces them**
- The words `scripts/check-ui-copy.mjs` forbids (`kanal(s)`, `team(s)`, `PMs`, `E2E(E)`, `end-to-end`, `encrypted`, `encryption`, `SRTP`, `X3DH`, `Signal Protocol`, `SQLCipher`, `AES-NNN`, `MLS`) appear in no string literal and no JSX text of `packages/ui/src`, `packages/web/src` or `packages/client-core/src`, tests and stories included. **This plan adds no surface that F10 allow-lists**, so `packages/web/src/strings/privacy.ts` is still not created and the lint is not touched. The upload tray never says how a file is protected (no "encrypting", "sealing", "sealed": DEV-W2-39); its phases are `reading`, `preparing`, `uploading`, `ready`, `failed`.
- Every user-visible string lives in `packages/web/src/strings/en.ts` and is passed to `@dilla/ui` as props; `@dilla/ui` components added here hard-code no English except overridable `aria-label` defaults. Casing (Q14): lower-case labels in the chrome (the toolbar, reaction names, tray phases, the reply chip, the mention list, card actions, the pins button), sentence case on dialog surfaces (the delete dialog, the pins dialog's heading and empty text, the lightbox's buttons, the tray's refusals). No exclamation marks; no "secure", "safe", "protected", "private"; no lock glyph.
- No string promises what web-2b cannot do: a pin is visible to everyone in the conversation and anyone in it may unpin it (Q20; the pins dialog says who pinned); a delete reaches devices that come online later (the instance keeps the type-2 envelope), but a copy someone saved stays theirs; a browser opens and sends files of at most 25 MB (`shell.drop.body`, `shell.tray.tooLarge`, `shell.attachment.tooLarge`).
- A client never switches on a server `detail` text: every mapping from a refusal to a string is by `code` and `status`. `packages/web/src/copy.test.ts`'s detail-switch grep stays green.
- Exact strings are fixed once in **L-COPY-03**; task 8 copies them into `docs/design/flows/04-conversation.md`'s Copy table, which **becomes the record** from then on (the web-2a lesson, its card 38: a later change is made in flow 04 and `en.ts` together, and `copy.test.ts`'s flow-table test, extended to flow 04 by task 9, holds them equal).

**Accessibility rules (WCAG 2.2 AA)** — as web-1 and web-2a (tokens only from `packages/design-tokens`; three themes `mesh`, `light`, `high-contrast` and reduced motion; a story per state; `vitest-axe`; the Storybook test-runner's axe gate incl. `target-size` for `Conversation/` and the focus-ring guard; 24×24 CSS px targets; `aria-disabled` not `disabled` for blocked controls; text children only). Additions fixed here:
- **Keyboard map of the conversation** (no single-character key anywhere, 2.1.4; no new modifier shortcut, Q14). The web-1 shell order (skip link → rail → channel list → header → log → composer → status bar) stays; the header gains the `pinned` button after the topic. The log becomes **one tab stop with a roving active row**: `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` move the active row, `Home`/`End` go to the first and last loaded row, entering the log focuses the active row (initially the newest). Only the active row's controls are tabbable (every interactive descendant of another row renders `tabIndex={-1}`; pointers still work), in this order after the row itself: the toolbar (one stop, `role="toolbar"`, `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`, `Home`/`End`), the reply reference's jump button, the attachment cards (one button each), the reaction bar (one stop, `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` across its chips and the add button); `Escape` inside any of them returns focus to the row; `Escape` on a row moves focus to the composer (web-1). The emoji grid is a popover dialog of 32 buttons in 8 columns with two-dimensional arrows, `Home`/`End`, `Enter`/`Space` to pick, `Escape` to close; focus returns to the control that opened it. The inline editor: `Enter` saves, `Shift+Enter` breaks the line, `Escape` cancels, IME-safe as the composer; focus returns to the row. In the composer: `ArrowUp` with an empty value and no open mention list edits the newest own ok message (focus to its editor); `Escape` with the mention list open closes it, else with a reply chip cancels the reply; the mention list is a combobox popup on the textarea (`role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant` are rendered **only while the list is open**; while it is closed the textarea keeps its web-1 `textbox` role and name, so `getByRole('textbox', { name: 'message #…' })` and the e2e `composerBox` keep resolving; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` move, `Enter` or `Tab` picks, `Escape` closes). The lightbox: `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` move between the images of the same message, `Escape` closes, focus returns to the card. Dropping files is pointer-only; the attach button and paste into the composer are the keyboard paths.
- Every action is reachable without hover: the toolbar is visible on `:hover`, on `:focus-within`, and on the active row **while focus is inside the log** (`.d-message-log:focus-within .d-message-row[data-active="true"]`), so it never floats over the previous row while the person types in the composer; inside the shell's narrow container (`@container d-shell (max-width: 47.99rem)`, the breakpoint `packages/ui/src/styles/base.css:32` already defines) the toolbar is in flow under the row's head (`position: static`), as flow 04's 360×740 wireframe shows; a touch target is never smaller than 24×24 (a `Button` of `size="sm"` is 22 px tall, `Button.css:9`, and is never used for a conversation control).
- The log is `role="log"` with `aria-live="polite"` and **`aria-relevant="additions"`**; the emoji grid is never rendered inside the log (it is a popover in the conversation's overlay layer, outside `role="log"`), so reaction counts, the grid's 32 names and pending-state text changes are not read as log additions. Residual, stated in flow 04 § Announcements: a newly inserted node inside a row (a first reaction chip, the inline editor, a pending-action line) may be read once by a screen reader as an addition.
- Reaction chips are `<button aria-pressed>` named `{name}, {count}` (`shell.message.reaction`); a mention is a text span styled as a pill (`--mention` for the own user, an outline for `@everyone`/`@here`/roles) whose text is its `@` name, never the raw token; an image card's `<img alt>` is the file's shown name; a pending action is announced through the row's state text, never by colour alone.
- Motion: the reply jump scrolls and flashes the target for 1.4 s (brief:186) and does not animate under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (the flash becomes a static outline for the same 1.4 s).
- F16 artefacts: tasks 8 and 9 run `packages/ui/scripts/shoot-stories.mjs` and leave PNGs of every new story in all three themes under `target/ui-screens/web-2b/`; the supervisor attaches them to the review, and task 11 makes the `ui` job upload them. Because `shoot-stories.mjs` fails only on a prefix that matches no story (`:18-26`), every SHOTS line names **one prefix per new story title** (task 8: `conversation-messagetoolbar-- conversation-reactionbar-- conversation-emojigrid-- conversation-messageeditor-- conversation-replychip-- conversation-mentionlist-- conversation-pinsdialog-- conversation-attachmenttray-- conversation-attachmentcard-- conversation-lightbox-- conversation-dropoverlay-- conversation-messagerow-- conversation-composer-- conversation-messagelog-- shell-channelheader--with-pins-button`; task 9: `screens-conversation--`), so a missing or renamed story fails the step. The screenshot viewport is 1280×800 (`shoot-stories.mjs:16`); the narrow layout reaches the founder through task 9's `Screens/Conversation` story `Narrow`, which renders the conversation inside a 360×740 frame. Task 8 writes `docs/design/flows/04-conversation.md` (wireframes at 1280×800 and 360×740, states, focus order and copy) before any component.

**Testing**
- TDD in every implementation task: the failing test first, its recorded failure, the implementation, the passing run, one commit.
- **A test must be able to fail (lesson a).** For each security- or correctness-critical assertion the task names the mutation that turns it red and has one step that applies it, shows the red run, and reverts it. The task index names the mutation.
- **Every new refusal states its attacker (lesson e).** A task that adds a refusal writes, next to the test, who can trigger it against an honest party and why they cannot. The ledger carries the statement for each refusal and each "ignored" fold rule this plan adds.
- **The model answers what the server answers (lesson f).** Every server behaviour a TypeScript task relies on is added to the double the tests of that route family use, in task 6: the delivery-service delete (membership, uploader user, 204/404) to `ModelDs` and `FakeServer`; the blob PUT/GET/DELETE and the confirm route (hash check, reference, uploader-only, pending sweep, 404, 413, and injected 429/507/410) to `FakeServer`; and to the native peer where the e2e drives it (task 5).
- **The migration is tested on old stores (lesson g).** Task 2 opens the committed v1 fixture (`app_v1.db`, → v3) and a new committed v2 fixture (`app_v2.db`, written by an ignored generator from the v2 DDL kept in the test crate, holding type 1–6 rows), and asserts the v3 shape and the folded result.
- **Parity fixtures.** `core/dilla-core/tests/fixtures/group_apply_parity.json` stays at eight cases and both `8` assertions stay (no `group_apply` result shape changes). The fold rules get their own fixture, `core/dilla-core/tests/fixtures/fold_parity.json` (L-CORE-39): six cases written by task 2, a seventh by task 3, asserted against the real core (`client_fold.rs`) and against `ModelCore` (task 6's `fold-parity.test.ts`); both assert the exact count. Fold behaviour the view cannot show (the blanking of hidden edit rows, the reaction cap, the replay rule) is mirrored by a named Rust unit test in task 2 and a named `model.test.ts` case in task 6 with the same inputs and assertions.
- **Mechanism, not duration, for cost (lesson c).** Where a rule bounds work an attacker could inflate (the fold's per-row cost, a download's body size), the test asserts the mechanism (the query plan uses the named index; the body read stops at the bound), never an elapsed time.
- The module-wide Go command is pinned and never narrowed at a block boundary: `/home/thim/.local/go/bin/go -C /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol test -race -shuffle=on -timeout 15m ./...`. A Go test that cannot run under the race detector is listed in `NON_RACE_STEP` of `scripts/check-ci-workflow.mjs` and in the `go` job's non-race step in the same task (none is expected).
- TypeScript unit tests of `@dilla/client-core` and `@dilla/web` never load the wasm: `FakeCore` (account half) and `ModelCore` with `ModelDs` (group half) stand in. WebCrypto in vitest is Node 24's `globalThis.crypto.subtle`; `OffscreenCanvas` and `createImageBitmap` do not exist there, so the thumbnail module takes them as injected dependencies and its real-browser path is proven by task 7's core-worker spec.
- **Browser thresholds (lesson c).** The CI runner has 4 vCPUs and is 3–5× slower than the dev machine: a browser test waits for a state, never a duration; every wait has an explicit timeout ≥ 30 s locally / 90 s in CI (`e2e/web/support/app.ts` `WAIT`); no assertion is an upper bound on elapsed time; `workers: 1`, `retries: 0`. A negative assertion ("the peer's edit changed nothing") waits for a later positive control (a following message from the same peer appears), never a duration.
- **Every browser test closes what it opens (lesson d).** Second contexts open through `e2e/web/support/second.ts` (web suite) and `second-harness.ts` (core-worker suite), which close in `finally`; web-driver children are closed; every `blob:` URL a test creates in the page is revoked by the page itself.
- CI is fail-closed: no `|| true`, no `continue-on-error`, no `if: always()` on a gate step; every `upload-artifact` sets `if-no-files-found: error`.

**Execution environment**

- `TMPDIR` is `/home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/.superpowers/tmp`. That path is too long for Chromium's socket files, so browser profile directories are never under it: persistent Playwright contexts use `/tmp/dw/<project>-<worker>` (and a second browser `/tmp/dw/<project>-<worker>-b`), created and removed by the fixtures; the test host's data directory is `/tmp/dw/host-<port>`.
- Fixed ports, one owner each. Existing: 5178 (facade spike and `e2e/tests`), 6006 (Storybook test-runner), 8443/8444, 5179, 7880/7882, 8453/8454 (core-worker suite), 8463/8464 (web suite), 8471/8472 (`docs:shots`), 6016–6024 (earlier screenshot runs). New: **6025** (task 8) and **6026** (task 9), each the screenshot script's static server for that task only. Go tests bind port 0. 5432 is opened only by the optional Postgres container.
- WebKit cannot launch on the dev host; it is gated in CI only (`webkit-web` keeps its two web-1 specs; this plan adds none to it).
- **A wiped store needs a page reload** (web-2a, `sahpool.rs:964-971`); nothing in this plan wipes a store.

- Race-gated Go tests are listed in the non-race step (none expected).

**Protocol-edit rules**
- Every edit to a `protocol/*.md` document gets its `protocol/07-versioning.md` change-table row in the same task and commit, appended as the last row in the table's form (`| date | e2ee 1, media 1, wire 1 | **Behaviour change.** … |` or `**Additive.** …`), and is listed in "Protocol and spec edits in this plan". No version axis is bumped: no client has shipped (07 precedent), and every edit here is additive, documents behaviour of this build, or changes a shape no released client reads.
- 07 step 4 (the founder's approval and a recorded independent review) is recorded as provisional on the rulings of `facts/rulings.md`, as for F1–F18 and web-2a.
- `npm run check:docs` stays green after every protocol edit. `protocol/vectors/*` is never edited by hand: the generator writes it.

**Commits**
- One commit per task, conventional subject (`docs(protocol): …`, `feat(core): …`, `feat(wasm): …`, `feat(store): …`, `feat(api): …`, `feat(testkit): …`, `feat(client-core): …`, `feat(ui): …`, `feat(web): …`, `test(e2e): …`, `ci: …`, `docs: …`), made by the supervisor in one command line: `git -C /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol commit -s -m "<subject>" -m "<body>" --trailer "Co-Authored-By: Codex <noreply@openai.com>" --trailer "Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XLFud8eoDaqf8uiZq5wjuP"`. The final paragraph of every commit message is therefore the two trailer lines `Co-Authored-By: Codex <noreply@openai.com>` and `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XLFud8eoDaqf8uiZq5wjuP` followed by the `Signed-off-by` that `-s` adds. A `-m` value never spans two lines, and the trailers are never passed as `-m` paragraphs.
- Task 11 may end in more than one commit: a red first CI run is fixed by further commits inside the task; the workflow runs on `pull_request`, so task 11 opens the plan's PR as a draft when it does not exist yet, and the green run's id goes into the PR description and `progress.md`.

## Interface ledger

The single source of truth for every interface that crosses a task boundary. A task text may add private helpers; it may not change a name, a type, a field order, a constant or an error code written here. If a drafter finds the code makes an entry impossible, the task says so in a "Ledger conflict" note at its top and the reviewer rules; the drafter does not silently adapt. Every interface the web-1 and web-2a ledgers fixed keeps its id and is cited, not restated, unless it changes here (then the change is stated under a new id with the old id named).

Conventions as web-1 and web-2a (`b12`, `b16`, `b32`, `b64`, `uint`, `tstr`, `x|null`; one deterministic CBOR item per boundary value; `_body` is the exact HTTP request body; timestamps are unix seconds; "hex" is lower-case). "The target" of a fold row is the message its `reply_to` names; **target resolution** in group `G` for msg id `X` is the status-0-or-2 row `SELECT … FROM app_messages WHERE group_id = G AND msg_id = X AND type = 0 ORDER BY seq LIMIT 1` (the earliest type-0 row carrying `X`: a later row that repeats a msg id — a replay, card 20 of web-1 — is shown as its own message but is never a target).

### L-CORE — `dilla-core`

**L-CORE-30 the envelope changes** (`src/envelope/mod.rs`; protocol/04 as edited by task 1)

```rust
/// Element 8 of an attachment: the file's name as the sender chose it, UTF-8, at most MAX_NAME bytes
/// ("" when the sender gives none). A receiver sanitises it for display and saving; it refuses only length.
pub const MAX_NAME: usize = 255;
pub struct Attachment { pub blob_id: [u8; 32], pub key: [u8; 32], pub nonce: [u8; 12], pub size: u64, pub mime: String,
    pub w: Option<u64>, pub h: Option<u64>, pub thumb: Option<Vec<u8>>, pub name: String }   // 9 elements on the wire, in this order
```

`decode` requires exactly 9 elements per attachment (`E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE` otherwise; an 8-element attachment is now refused — no released client wrote one). `validate` adds, in this order after the existing checks: `name.len() > MAX_NAME` → `E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT`; for `kind` ∈ 1..=6: `reply_to` is `None` → `E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`, a non-empty `attachments` or `previews` → `E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`. The Go readable receiver (`internal/api/envelope.go` `ParseEnvelope`) applies the same three rules with the same codes. **Attacker statement:** the new refusals reject only an envelope its own sender built wrongly; an honest client never sends a fold without a target or a fold carrying files, and no other member can make an honest member's envelope fail them.

Envelope vectors (`protocol/vectors/envelope.json`, generated): case 1 ("text message with a reply and one attachment") gains `name: "wolf-capes.jpg"` and is regenerated (new `cbor`, `length`, `commitment`); a fifth case **"image message with a thumbnail and a name"** (`msgId` 16×0x41, type 0, `replyTo` null, body `""`, one attachment `blobId` 32×0x43, `key` 32×0x44, `nonce` 12×0x45, `size` 1234, `mime` `image/png`, `w` 640, `h` 480, `thumb` the `thumb` bytes of `attachment.json` case 3, `name` `"map.png"`, `kf` 32×0x46); `rejects` gains, each with its code: **"an edit with no reply_to"** (`E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`), **"a reaction carrying an attachment"** (`E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`), **"an attachment name one byte over 255"** (`E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT`), **"an attachment of eight elements"** (`E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`). The Rust `run_rejects`, the Go `envelope_test.go` and the TS generator's own test read every reject.

**L-CORE-31 the attachment AEAD** (`src/attachment.rs`, new; protocol/04 § Attachments as written by task 1; Q15)

```rust
pub const AAD_BLOB: &[u8] = b"dilla attachment v1";
pub const AAD_THUMB: &[u8] = b"dilla thumb v1";
pub const TAG_LEN: usize = 16;
/// 8 192 (the envelope's thumb bound, on the sealed bytes) minus the tag.
pub const MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT: usize = 8_176;
/// nonce with byte 11 XOR 0x01.
pub fn thumb_nonce(nonce: &[u8; 12]) -> [u8; 12];
/// SHA-256 of the stored bytes.
pub fn blob_id(stored: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32];
/// AES-256-GCM(key, nonce, aad = AAD_BLOB) over the file; returns ct ‖ tag (plaintext length + 16 bytes).
pub fn seal_blob(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], plaintext: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>;
/// Order: blob_id(stored) != blob_id → E_BLOB_HASH; stored shorter than TAG_LEN or the AEAD fails → E_BLOB_OPEN;
/// plaintext length != size → E_BLOB_OPEN. Returns the plaintext.
pub fn open_blob(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], blob_id: &[u8; 32], size: u64, stored: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ProtocolError>;
/// AES-256-GCM(key, thumb_nonce(nonce), aad = AAD_THUMB); plaintext over MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT → E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT.
pub fn seal_thumb(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ProtocolError>;
/// The AEAD fails or thumb is shorter than TAG_LEN → E_BLOB_OPEN.
pub fn open_thumb(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], thumb: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ProtocolError>;
```

Byte layout (protocol/04): the stored blob is exactly `ciphertext ‖ tag` (no nonce prefix: the nonce travels in the envelope); `size` is the plaintext length; `blob_id = SHA-256(stored)`. The thumbnail is a WebP image (or a JPEG where the sender's platform cannot encode WebP), longest side ≤ 320 px, plaintext ≤ 8 176 bytes; a receiver renders a thumbnail only when its plaintext begins with `RIFF` and has `WEBP` at offset 8, or begins with `FF D8 FF`, and renders the full file as an image only when its `mime` is one of `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`, `image/gif`; everything else is a file to save.

`protocol/vectors/attachment.json` (generated by `packages/protocol-vectors/src/attachment.ts` with WebCrypto; read by `dilla_core::vectors::run_attachment`, by task 6's `crypto.test.ts`, and by the Go golden through the guest's `run_all`):

```json
{ "version": 1,
  "description": "protocol/04 § Attachments: AES-256-GCM, stored = ciphertext || 16-byte tag, blob_id = SHA-256(stored); thumb under the same key with nonce byte 11 XOR 0x01",
  "aad_blob": "<hex of 'dilla attachment v1'>", "aad_thumb": "<hex of 'dilla thumb v1'>",
  "cases": [ { "name": "…", "key": "<32 B>", "nonce": "<12 B>", "plaintext": "<hex>", "size": 0,
               "stored": "<hex: ct || tag>", "blob_id": "<32 B>",
               "thumb_nonce": "<12 B>", "thumb_plaintext": "<hex>|null", "thumb": "<hex>|null" } ],
  "rejects": [ { "name": "…", "kind": "blob|thumb", "key": "…", "nonce": "…", "blob_id": "<32 B, blob only>",
                 "size": 0, "data": "<hex>", "error": "E_BLOB_HASH|E_BLOB_OPEN" } ] }
```

Cases (exact inputs): 1 **"empty file"** key 32×0x51, nonce 12×0x52, plaintext empty, no thumb; 2 **"one byte"** key 32×0x53, nonce 12×0x54, plaintext `0x2a`, no thumb; 3 **"a 1000-byte file with a thumbnail"** key 32×0x55, nonce `000102030405060708090a0b`, plaintext bytes `i mod 251` for i in 0..1000, thumb plaintext = the 26 bytes `52494646` `12000000` `57454250` followed by 14 bytes `0x00` (a WebP header stub; vectors check bytes, not decoding); 4 **"a 300-byte file"** key 32×0x57, nonce 12×0x58, plaintext `(i * 7) mod 256` for i in 0..300, no thumb (adjudicated, AI-1: every byte of the file is embedded in the browser wasm through `vectors_check_json`, `core/dilla-core-wasm/src/lib.rs:129-152` and `vectors/mod.rs:28-32`, so a 70 000-byte case alone would exceed task 1's budget; AES-GCM's counter is position-independent and case 3 already spans 63 blocks; a native unit test `a_70000_byte_file_round_trips` in `src/attachment.rs` keeps the large-file round trip). Rejects (the four blob rejects derive from **case 2** (17 stored bytes), the thumb reject from case 3, as named): **"blob_id does not match"** (`blob_id` with byte 0 XOR 0x01 → `E_BLOB_HASH`), **"tag bit flipped"** (last byte of `stored` XOR 0x01 and `blob_id` recomputed over the changed bytes → `E_BLOB_OPEN`), **"sealed under the thumbnail AAD"** (case 2's plaintext sealed with `AAD_THUMB` and the blob nonce, `blob_id` over it → `E_BLOB_OPEN`), **"size disagrees"** (`size` = 2 → `E_BLOB_OPEN`), **"thumbnail sealed under the file's own nonce"** (kind `thumb`, `nonce` = case 3's nonce, `data` = case 3's thumbnail plaintext sealed with `AAD_THUMB` under that nonce **without** the byte-11 XOR, so `open_thumb`'s derived nonce does not open it → `E_BLOB_OPEN`), **"truncated below the tag"** (`stored` = 15 bytes of case 2's `stored`, `blob_id` over them → `E_BLOB_OPEN`). A `blob` reject carries `blob_id` and `size`; a `thumb` reject carries neither. The Rust suite name is `"attachment"`, sixth in `run_all` (`envelope, franking, sframe, identity, frames, attachment, rejects`; `"rejects"` stays last); its fields per case are `stored`, `blob_id`, `open`, `thumb`, `thumb_open` (absent fields are not counted; 14 in all), and every reject counts once in `"rejects"` named `attachment reject: <name>`. `Attachment`'s hand-written `Debug` prints `name` as `<n bytes>`, never its text. **Mutations named (task 1):** an empty AAD in `seal_blob` → case 1–4 `stored` go red; `open_blob` without the hash check → the `E_BLOB_HASH` reject goes red.

**L-CORE-32 error codes** — `ProtocolError::BlobOpen` with `code()` `"E_BLOB_OPEN"` and the reverse mapping; `E_BLOB_HASH` is now returned by `open_blob`. protocol/04's Error codes line becomes `E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`, `E_ENVELOPE_TYPE`, `E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT`, `E_FRANK_MISMATCH`, `E_BLOB_HASH`, `E_BLOB_OPEN`.

**L-SQL-30 app schema v3 and `migrate_app`** (`src/client/schema.rs`, `src/client/mod.rs`; amends web-2a L-CORE-20)

```sql
-- MIGRATE_V2_TO_V3 (run after APP_SCHEMA on a v2 store, and after MIGRATE_V1_TO_V2 on a v1 store)
ALTER TABLE app_messages ADD COLUMN reply_to  BLOB;                        -- envelope.reply_to of a status-0 row (16 bytes) or NULL
ALTER TABLE app_messages ADD COLUMN edit_body TEXT;                        -- the body of the edit applied to this type-0 row, NULL when none
ALTER TABLE app_messages ADD COLUMN edit_seq  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;  -- the seq of that edit, 0 when none
UPDATE app_meta SET v = x'03' WHERE k = 'schema';
-- new tables: created by APP_SCHEMA (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) on every store, fresh or old
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_reactions (
  group_id BLOB NOT NULL, target BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(target) = 16),
  user_id  BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(user_id) = 16), emoji TEXT NOT NULL, seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (group_id, target, user_id, emoji)) WITHOUT ROWID;           -- present reactions only; seq = the deciding type-3 row
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_pins (
  group_id BLOB NOT NULL, target BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(target) = 16), seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
  by_user BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(by_user) = 16), PRIMARY KEY (group_id, target)) WITHOUT ROWID;   -- present pins only
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_purges (
  group_id BLOB NOT NULL, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, channel_id BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(channel_id) = 16),
  blob_ids BLOB NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (group_id, seq)) WITHOUT ROWID;      -- blob_ids: deterministic CBOR [b32…]
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_roles (
  community_id BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(community_id) = 16), role_id BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(role_id) = 16),
  PRIMARY KEY (community_id, role_id)) WITHOUT ROWID;
-- APP_INDEXES_V3: run by migrate_conn after any migration, on every store whose schema is ≤ 3 (adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-02:
-- every refold statement is an index search, never a scan of the target's rows)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS app_messages_by_reply    ON app_messages (group_id, reply_to, type, sender_user, seq);  -- steps 2 and 3, the delete branch, the backfill
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS app_messages_by_pin      ON app_messages (group_id, reply_to, type, seq);               -- step 5: MAX(seq) per type 5 and 6
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS app_messages_by_reaction ON app_messages (group_id, reply_to, sender_user, body, seq);   -- step 4 per (user, emoji) and its GROUP BY
```

`APP_SCHEMA` creates `app_messages` with the three v3 columns inline (after `mention`), creates the four new tables, and seeds `INSERT OR IGNORE … ('schema', x'03')`; it still names no v2 or v3 column of an existing table in an index (`schema.rs:63-65`'s rule), which is why the three fold indexes live in `APP_INDEXES_V3` (`client_identity.rs`'s object list names `app_messages_by_pin`, `app_messages_by_reaction` and `app_messages_by_reply`). `migrate_conn(c) -> Result<u64, StorageError>`: run `APP_SCHEMA`; read `schema`; `1` → `MIGRATE_V1_TO_V2` then `MIGRATE_V2_TO_V3`; `2` → `MIGRATE_V2_TO_V3`; then, when the found value is ≤ 3, `APP_INDEXES_V3`; return the value found (`1`, `2`, `3`, or a larger value unchanged and nothing run after `APP_SCHEMA`). `migrate_app` and `ClientCore::open` run, in the one unit: found `1` → the v1→v2 backfill (web-2a, unchanged) then **`backfill_v3`**; found `2` → `backfill_v3`. `open` refuses a value above 3 with `E_CORE_STATE` "app schema <n> is newer than this build". `fn backfill_v3(u: &UnitScope<'_>) -> Result<(), StorageError>` (private to `client/mod.rs`; it loads no MLS group, so it takes no storage — AI-7): (a) for every `app_messages` row with `status = 0 AND envelope IS NOT NULL`, read `reply_to` **by a structural walk** (`stored_reply_to`: `decode_strict` of a nine-element CBOR array whose element 4 is a 16-byte bstr or null; nothing else of the envelope is validated) and set it when non-null; only bytes that are not such an array are `StorageError::Codec("app_messages envelope does not decode")` and roll the migration back; (b) for every distinct `(group_id, reply_to)` of a status-0 row with `type BETWEEN 1 AND 6 AND reply_to IS NOT NULL`, `refold(c, group_id, reply_to, &FoldScope::Full, None, None)`. Nothing else changes: `mention` flags stay as v2 set them, no purge is recorded, no role is known. **Attacker statement (adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-01 / AI-2):** web-2a's core stored as status 0 every envelope its decoder accepted, including types 1–6 with a null `reply_to` and eight-element attachments, which task 1's `Envelope::decode` now refuses and which any member can send a web-2a browser today; the structural walk accepts both, so the migration's only refusal is reached by bytes no core of this project wrote (a store this build did not write), never by a message another member sent. The test `a_v2_row_this_build_refuses_still_migrates` seeds both legacy shapes into a v2 copy and opens it. **Mutations named:** (a) skip `MIGRATE_V2_TO_V3` when the found schema is 2 → the v2-fixture test fails at open with `E_CORE_STORAGE` naming the missing column `reply_to` (the first statement to meet it is `APP_INDEXES_V3`'s index, TESTS-13); (f) make `stored_reply_to` call `Envelope::decode` (its error mapped to the same `Codec`) → `a_v2_row_this_build_refuses_still_migrates` fails at `expect("open")` with `E_CORE_STORAGE`; (g) make the timeline's attachment summary propagate `Envelope::decode`'s error → the same test fails at its `timeline` call.

**L-CORE-33 the fold** (`src/client/fold.rs`; Q18, Q19, Q20; the protocol/04 semantics task 1 writes)

```rust
/// Recomputes what `scope` covers of everything folded onto the target `msg_id` of `group_id`, from the stored rows,
/// inside the caller's unit. `trigger` is the row whose insert caused the call (None from the backfill and from deletes
/// by seq); `own` is the device's identity (None from the backfill and from deletes by seq). Idempotent.
/// Visibility pub(super) (adjudicated, AI-3 / INTERFACES-10): `Own` is private to `client` (`client/mod.rs:40`), so a
/// pub(crate) item naming it fails `private_interfaces` under -D warnings; every caller is inside `client`.
pub(super) fn refold(c: &rusqlite::Connection, group_id: &[u8; 16], target: &[u8; 16], scope: &FoldScope,
    trigger: Option<&FoldTrigger>, own: Option<&Own>) -> Result<(), StorageError>;
pub(super) struct FoldTrigger { pub seq: u64, pub ty: u8, pub sender_user: [u8; 16], pub sender_device: [u8; 16] }
/// Which steps a call recomputes (adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-02). Steps 1 and 2 run for every scope.
pub(super) enum FoldScope { Full, Edit, Reaction { user: [u8; 16], emoji: String }, Pin }
/// type 1 → Edit; types 3 and 4 with a sender → Reaction { user: sender_user, emoji: body }; types 5 and 6 → Pin;
/// type 0, type 2, None, or a 3/4 row without a sender → Full.
pub(super) fn scope_of(ty: Option<i64>, sender_user: Option<[u8; 16]>, body: &str) -> FoldScope;
pub(super) fn resolve(c: &rusqlite::Connection, group_id: &[u8; 16], msg_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<Option<Target>, StorageError>;
pub(super) fn target_of(ty: Option<i64>, msg_id: Option<[u8; 16]>, reply_to: Option<[u8; 16]>) -> Option<[u8; 16]>;
```

Task 2 binds `trigger` and `own` as `_trigger`/`_own` and marks `FoldTrigger` `#[allow(dead_code)] // task 3's purge record reads the fields`; task 3 renames them and removes the attribute (AI-3). Task 3's checks call `fold::resolve` (no second resolver, INTERFACES-10).

Called: after every status-0 insert with `type` 1..=6 (with its `reply_to` as the target, `scope_of` of the inserted row, and a trigger), after every status-0 type-0 insert (with its own `msg_id` as the target and `FoldScope::Full`: a fold that waited for it applies now), and after every row a delete by seq turns to status 2 (`message_deleted` and a served `deleted = 1`: with the row's `msg_id` as the target when it was type 0, or with its `reply_to` when it was type 1..=6; `scope_of` of the row as it was stored before the update — its `type`, `sender_user` and `body` are read before the UPDATE blanks them; no trigger). The backfill uses `FoldScope::Full`. The paths are: `sync.rs` received insert, `sync.rs` `apply_message` own adoption and deleted marker, `messages.rs` `send_confirm`. Steps, in this order, all reading only `status = 0` rows unless said; step 3 runs for `Full` and `Edit`, step 4 for `Full` (all pairs) and `Reaction` (that pair only), step 5 for `Full` and `Pin`:
1. Resolve the target `T` (ledger conventions). None → **for `Full` and `Edit` only**: for every distinct `sender_user` `U` of a status-0 type-2 row with `reply_to = target`, set `body = '', envelope = NULL` on every status-0 type-1 row with `reply_to = target` and `sender_user = U` (adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-03: a device that was offline across the send and the delivery service's tombstone stores the target as an empty row with no `msg_id`, `sync.rs:138-172`, and would otherwise keep the author's edits in plaintext forever); nothing else is written (the fold rows wait; they stay stored and hidden). **Attacker statement:** only a user's own type-2 row blanks only that user's own edits, so no member can blank another member's words. `T.status = 1` cannot happen (a status-1 row has no `msg_id`).
2. **Delete wins.** `deleted` := `T.status = 2` or a type-2 row with `reply_to = target` and `sender_user = T.sender_user` exists. When `deleted`: (task 3) **record the purge** first when all hold — `trigger.ty = 2`, `own` is Some, `trigger.sender_device = own.device_id`, `trigger.sender_user = own.user_id = T.sender_user`, `T.status = 0` — as `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO app_purges (group_id, seq, channel_id, blob_ids)` with `seq = T.seq`, `channel_id = app_groups.target_id` of the group, `blob_ids` = the CBOR array of the `blob_id`s of `T`'s envelope attachments (possibly empty), read **by a structural walk** of the stored envelope (element 6 an array; element 0 of each entry a 32-byte bstr), and on any walk failure recorded as the empty array instead of failing the unit (adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-06: a stored envelope the v3 decoder refuses must never make the type-2 row unconfirmable or stall `group_apply`); then `T` becomes `status = 2, body = '', envelope = NULL, reason = '', edit_body = NULL, edit_seq = 0`; every type-1 row with `reply_to = target` gets `body = '', envelope = NULL`; `app_reactions` and `app_pins` rows of the target are deleted. Stop.
3. **Edit.** `E` := the highest-`seq` type-1 row with `reply_to = target` and `sender_user = T.sender_user`. `T.edit_body, T.edit_seq` := `E.body, E.seq`, or `NULL, 0` when none. The `mention` flag is not touched (an edit never raises a mention).
4. **Reactions, per user.** For each `(sender_user, body)` among type-3 and type-4 rows with `reply_to = target`, the highest-`seq` row decides: type 3 → `(group_id, target, sender_user, body, seq)` is in `app_reactions`; type 4 or none → it is not. `Full`: delete the target's `app_reactions` rows and insert from one `SELECT sender_user, body, type, MAX(seq) … WHERE group_id = ?1 AND reply_to = ?2 AND status = 0 AND type IN (3, 4) GROUP BY sender_user, body` keeping the groups whose max row is type 3 (SQLite's bare-column rule for `MAX`; no correlated `NOT EXISTS`). `Reaction { user, emoji }`: `SELECT type, seq … WHERE group_id = ?1 AND reply_to = ?2 AND sender_user = ?3 AND body = ?4 AND status = 0 AND type IN (3, 4) ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1`, then upsert or delete that one `app_reactions` row.
5. **Pins, from any member** (Q20). The highest-`seq` type-5 or type-6 row with `reply_to = target` decides, read as two index searches `SELECT MAX(seq) … AND type = 5` and `… AND type = 6` (then the winning row's `sender_user` by seq): type 5 → upsert `app_pins (group_id, target, seq, by_user = its sender_user)`; type 6 or none → delete the row.

Every statement of steps 1–5 is a `pub(super) const` in `fold.rs`; a unit test inside `fold.rs` runs `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on each against a connection holding `APP_SCHEMA` and `APP_INDEXES_V3` and asserts that no plan line contains `SCAN app_messages` (each is a `SEARCH … USING [COVERING] INDEX app_messages_by_…`). **Cost (lesson c, mechanism not duration):** an insert-triggered refold is a constant number of index searches, so a catch-up of n fold rows on one target costs O(n log n); a `Full` refold (a type-0 or type-2 insert, the backfill) is one pass over the target's fold rows.

Every received fold row is still stored as its own `app_messages` row with its type and body (web-1 rule) and listed in `new_seqs`; the timeline never shows it (L-CORE-34). **Attacker statements.** An edit or delete from anyone but the target's author changes nothing (steps 2–3 compare `sender_user`, which the MLS credential authenticates, `sync.rs:606`); a member cannot remove or forge another member's reaction (step 4 is keyed by the authenticated sender); a pin or unpin from any member is accepted (Q20's recorded deviation: no client holds a role snapshot; the pins dialog names who pinned); a fold row aimed at a msg id the device does not hold costs only the row the device stores anyway; a replayed type-0 row that copies an existing msg id never becomes a target. Nothing here refuses: a fold that fails a rule is ignored, never an error. **Mutations named:** (task 2) compare `sender_device` instead of `sender_user` in step 3 → the "an edit from the author's other device applies" test goes red; drop the `sender_user` comparison in step 2 → the fold-parity case "an edit by another user is ignored"'s companion "a delete by another user is ignored" unit test goes red; key step 4 by device → "reactions are per user" (two devices of one user, one chip of count 1) goes red; skip step 1's unheld branch → `a_delete_of_a_target_never_held_blanks_its_authors_edits` (the raw peer sends T, an edit of T and a type 2 of T, the relay tombstones T, me applies all in one `group_apply`; the edit row's body is `""` and its envelope NULL, and a type-1 row of another user naming T keeps its body) goes red; reduce `APP_INDEXES_V3` to the single index `app_messages_by_reply ON app_messages (group_id, reply_to)` → `every_fold_statement_is_an_index_search` goes red (the step-3 and step-4 statements lose their `type=? AND sender_user=?` and `sender_user=? AND body=?` constraints); (task 3) record a purge without the `trigger.sender_device = own.device_id` clause → "a delete received from the own user's other device records no purge" goes red.

```rust
pub fn purge_done(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], seq: u64) -> Result<(), ClientError>;
```

The purge condition's `T.status = 0` clause is proven by its own test (adjudicated, TESTS-10): two type-2 requests for the same own message are prepared while it is status 0, the first is confirmed, `purge_done` runs, then the second is confirmed: `purges()` stays empty; **mutation named (task 3):** drop `T.status = 0` from the purge condition → that test goes red.

**L-CORE-39 the fold parity fixture** (`core/dilla-core/tests/fixtures/fold_parity.json`, version 1)

```json
{ "v": 1, "cases": [ { "name": "…", "rows": [ { "seq": 2, "what": "peer-target" } ], "through": 3,
  "view": [ [2, 0, "the target", 0, [["👍", 1, 0]], 0] ], "hidden": [3] } ] }
```

Common start: web-2a's parity start (me registered, the raw peer joined by external commit at seq 1, me applied it). `rows` are message rows in seq order, built by `what`: `peer-target` (the peer's type-0 body `the target`, msg id 16×0x71), `own-target` (me's type-0 body `my target` through `send_prepare` and its echo adopted from the outbox; its msg id is the case's target), `peer-edit` (type 1, body `edited by the peer`), `peer-react` / `peer-unreact` (type 3 / 4, body `👍`), `peer-delete` (type 2), `peer-pin` (type 5), `peer-react-unheld` (type 3 `👍` with `reply_to` 16×0xee), and task 3's `own-react` (me's type 3 `👍` through the generalised `send_prepare`, its echo adopted); every fold row's `reply_to` is the case's target. Rows are built in order; **before an own fold row (`own-react`) the rows built so far are applied with `group_apply(…, its seq − 1)`** (L-CORE-36 refuses a fold whose target is not held), then it is prepared, framed and uploaded without a confirm (its echo is adopted later); `own-target` needs no early apply. Both runners (Rust `client_fold.rs`, TS `fold-parity.test.ts`) use this rule (adjudicated, A2 / peer-client 2). After the final `group_apply(…, through)`, `timeline(G, 0, 200)` must contain, for each `view` entry `[seq, status, body, edited_seq, reactions, pinned]`, the row at that seq with those elements (11, 12, 14, 15 of L-CORE-34; `mine` relative to me), and must contain no row whose seq is in `hidden`. Cases (task 2 writes 1–6; task 3 appends 7; the Rust runner in `client_fold.rs` and task 6's TS runner assert the exact count):

| # | name | rows | view | hidden |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | an edit by the author replaces the body | 2 peer-target, 3 peer-edit | `[2, 0, "edited by the peer", 3, [], 0]` | `[3]` |
| 2 | an edit by another user is ignored | 2 own-target, 3 peer-edit | `[2, 0, "my target", 0, [], 0]` | `[3]` |
| 3 | a reaction is kept per user and removed by its sender | 2 peer-target, 3 peer-react, 4 peer-unreact, 5 peer-react | `[2, 0, "the target", 0, [["👍", 1, 0]], 0]` | `[3, 4, 5]` |
| 4 | a delete by the author removes the target and what folded onto it | 2 peer-target, 3 peer-react, 4 peer-edit, 5 peer-delete | `[2, 2, "", 0, [], 0]` | `[3, 4, 5]` |
| 5 | a pin is accepted from any member | 2 own-target, 3 peer-pin | `[2, 0, "my target", 0, [], 1]` | `[3]` |
| 6 | a fold whose target is not held changes nothing | 2 peer-target, 3 peer-react-unheld | `[2, 0, "the target", 0, [], 0]` | `[3]` |
| 7 | an own reaction folds when its upload is adopted | 2 peer-target, 3 own-react, 4 peer-react | `[2, 0, "the target", 0, [["👍", 2, 1]], 0]` | `[3, 4]` |

### L-SQL — dillad store

**L-SQL-31 pending references** (both engines; migration `00014_blob_refs_pending.sql` with its schema twin `schema/012_blob_refs_pending.sql`, held equal by `internal/store/schema_test.go`)

```sql
-- SQLite (blob_refs is STRICT)
ALTER TABLE blob_refs ADD COLUMN confirmed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (confirmed IN (0, 1));
CREATE INDEX blob_refs_pending ON blob_refs (created) WHERE confirmed = 0;
-- Postgres
ALTER TABLE blob_refs ADD COLUMN confirmed SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (confirmed IN (0, 1));
CREATE INDEX blob_refs_pending ON blob_refs (created) WHERE confirmed = 0;
-- goose Down: DROP INDEX blob_refs_pending; ALTER TABLE blob_refs DROP COLUMN confirmed;
```

Every reference that exists when the migration runs is confirmed (the default), so nothing stored before this plan is ever swept as pending.

```go
// store.Blobs gains
PutPendingBlobRef(ctx context.Context, blobID []byte, channelID, uploaderDevice id.ID, mime string, created int64) error // INSERT … confirmed = 0 … ON CONFLICT (blob_id, channel_id) DO NOTHING
ConfirmBlobRef(ctx context.Context, blobID []byte, channelID id.ID) error   // UPDATE … SET confirmed = 1; ErrNotFound when no row
ListPendingBlobRefs(ctx context.Context, before int64, limit int32) ([]BlobRefRow, error) // confirmed = 0 AND created < before ORDER BY created, channel_id, blob_id LIMIT limit
// BlobRefRow gains `Confirmed bool`; every query that reads blob_refs rows selects it.
```

`PutBlobRef` keeps writing confirmed references (its existing callers are tests and fixtures). The literal `Blobs` method list of `internal/store/contract_test.go` gains the three names. **Mutation named (task 4):** make `PutPendingBlobRef` write `confirmed = 1` → "an upload never confirmed is swept after pending_ttl" goes red.

### L-HTTP — routes

Common to every new row as web-2a's L-HTTP preamble: CBOR answers and refusals; `401 E_UNAUTHENTICATED` without a valid token; `403` for a pending or provisional scope as `auth.Sessions.Middleware` answers; `429` and `500` can always be answered.

**L-HTTP-80 `DELETE /v1/groups/{id}/messages/{seq}` is member-only** (changed; Q19; DEV-W2-09; `internal/ds/message.go`) — `DeleteMessage` calls `d.requireMember(ctx, groupID, s)` as its first store access after the `seq` bound: a caller whose device is not a current member of the group is `404 E_NOT_FOUND` (the answer every member-only group route gives, so group existence is not probeable), before the uploader rule (`403 E_NOT_UPLOADER`) and the not-found row (`404`). Everything else is unchanged: the tombstone, op 21 `message.deleted [seq, deleted_at]` fanned to the group with replay, and `204`. **Attacker statement:** the new refusal hits only a device that is no longer in the group; its user's other member devices can still delete, and a removed device can no longer address the group in any other way either.

**L-HTTP-81 `PUT /v1/channels/{id}/blobs/{blob_id}` writes a pending reference** (changed; Q17; `internal/api/blobs.go`) — a reference the PUT creates is written by `PutPendingBlobRef` (`confirmed = 0`); a PUT into a channel that already holds a reference to these bytes adds nothing and leaves it as it was (confirmed or not). Every status, header, meter and quota rule is unchanged; a pending reference is readable (`GET`/`HEAD`) and deletable like a confirmed one.

**L-HTTP-82 `POST /v1/channels/{id}/blobs/{blob_id}/confirm`** (new; `internal/api/blobs.go` `Register`) — auth **E**; no body (`Content-Length` 0 or an empty body; a body is ignored); `channel(r, PermViewChannel)` (so `404` for a caller who may not view the channel, `403` for a category); bytes an administrator purged → `410 E_PRUNED`; no reference in this channel → `404 E_NOT_FOUND`; the reference's uploader device belongs to another user (read as the DELETE reads it) → `403 E_NOT_UPLOADER`; else one `Tx` that first takes `LockBlob(blob_id)` and then runs `ConfirmBlobRef` (`ErrNotFound` inside → `404`: the reference was dropped meanwhile), and `204`. Idempotent: confirming a confirmed reference is `204`. **Attacker statement:** only the uploading user can confirm or fail to confirm their own reference; nobody else's action can make an honest upload expire.

**L-HTTP-83 the pending sweep** (`internal/blob/gc.go`; `blobs.pending_ttl`, default `24h`, `0` turns it off) — `NewSweeper(repo store.Repository, s *Store, clk clock.Clock, grace, pendingTTL, interval time.Duration, log *slog.Logger)`; each sweep's `expireReferences` also drops, with reason `"pending"`, the references `ListPendingBlobRefs(now − pendingTTL, sweepBatch)` returns, each through a private `dropPendingReference` (not `dropReference`, which deletes the row it was handed, `gc.go:209-226`): one `Tx` that takes `LockBlob(blob_id)`, re-reads the reference with `GetBlobRef` and **skips it when it is confirmed or gone**, else deletes it and marks its blob unreferenced when it was the last (which `gc_grace` then collects as today) (adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-05 / A4: a reference listed as pending and confirmed by its uploader before the drop would otherwise be deleted after the client's confirm returned 204). The re-read is the tested guard (`TestAReferenceConfirmedAfterTheListingIsKept`, whose repository wrapper confirms what the listing returns; **mutation named:** drop without the re-read → red). The lock closes the remaining Postgres window between the re-read and the delete (a confirm waits on the `blobs` row lock and then answers 404, which the client reports as `E_ATTACHMENT_MISSING`); SQLite's single writer already serialises both; the lock is defence in depth and is not separately tested (TESTS-09); `cmd/dillad/serve.go:228` passes `cfg.Blobs.PendingTTL.Value()`; `internal/obs/metrics.go`'s `BlobRefExpired` doc names `"pending"`. **Attacker statement:** the sweep removes only references their own uploader never confirmed; the honest client confirms before it sends the message that names them (L-TS-34), so a sent attachment is never pending. **Mutation named (task 4):** sweep without the `confirmed = 0` clause → "a confirmed reference outlives pending_ttl" goes red.

**L-HTTP-84 the CSP row** (`internal/web/web.go`; Q17; DEV-W2-42) — `cspHead` becomes `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' blob:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'`; `cspTail` is unchanged (`media-src 'none'` stays). The four Go pins and `e2e/web/csp-axe.spec.ts:10` change with it; protocol/09's header block and its sentence ("web-1 grants no … `blob:` image") change to say web-2b grants `blob:` images for attachments the client opens, and nothing else.

**L-HTTP-90…95 route helpers** (`packages/client-core/src/http/routes.ts`, on `class Routes`; task 6)

| id | function | route | auth, bucket, idempotent | request | returns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 90 | `deleteGroupMessage(groupId, seq)` | `DELETE /v1/groups/{id}/messages/{seq}` | E, `write`, yes; `ok: [204, 404]` | — | `'deleted' \| 'gone'` (204 / 404) |
| 91 | `putBlob(channelId, blobId, stored)` | `PUT /v1/channels/{id}/blobs/{hex}` | E, **`upload`**, yes | the stored bytes, `contentType: 'application/octet-stream'`, not copied | `{ created: boolean; size: number }` (201 → true, 200 → false); refusals propagate as `DillaHttpError` |
| 92 | `confirmBlob(channelId, blobId)` | `POST …/blobs/{hex}/confirm` | E, `write`, yes | no body | `void` (204); 404/403/410 propagate |
| 93 | `getBlob(channelId, blobId, maxBytes?: number)` | `GET …/blobs/{hex}` | E, `read`, yes; `ok: [200, 404]` | — | `Uint8Array \| null` (404 → null); `maxBytes` is passed to the transport as `HttpRequest.maxBodyBytes` (adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-13) |
| 94 | `deleteBlob(channelId, blobId)` | `DELETE …/blobs/{hex}` | E, `write`, yes; `ok: [204, 404]` | — | `void`; a 403 propagates |
| 95 | `listMembers(communityId)` (web-1 row 32, changed) | — | — | — | `MemberRow` gains `roleIds: Uint8Array[]` (element 3 of the member row) |

`HttpRequest` gains `contentType?: 'application/cbor' | 'application/octet-stream'` (default `'application/cbor'`); for `'application/octet-stream'` the body is handed to `fetch` as given (no `.slice()`: a 25 MiB body is not copied twice). `HttpRequest` also gains `maxBodyBytes?: number`: when set, a 2xx response whose `Content-Length` exceeds it, or whose body (read from `response.body` chunk by chunk instead of `arrayBuffer()`, `client.ts:64`) passes it, is cancelled and rejects with `DillaHttpError({ status: <the response status>, code: 'E_BODY_TOO_LARGE', detail: 'the response body is larger than <n> bytes', retryAfterMs: null, extra: [] })`, never retried. A non-2xx response is always bounded by `max(64 KiB, maxBodyBytes ?? 0)` using the same streamed check, even when `maxBodyBytes` is unset. `fetchAttachment` passes `d.size + 16` (the stored length of a sealed file) and maps `E_BODY_TOO_LARGE` to `AttachmentError('E_BLOB_OPEN', 'the stored object is larger than its descriptor')` before any hashing; a test serves `size + 17` bytes and expects that refusal. **Attacker statement:** only an instance (or a member who uploaded a lying descriptor, whose own message then fails to open) can trigger it; an honest upload's stored length is exactly `size + 16`. `Bucket` gains `'upload'` and `PACING.upload = { perSecond: 16 / 60, burst: 16 }` (80 % of the per-user 20 a minute, `blobmeter.go`). `SyncRoutes` is unchanged (L-TS-31).

```ts
export interface TrayEntry { id: string; name: string; size: number; mime: string; image: boolean; phase: TrayPhase; reason: string; descriptor: AttachmentDescriptor | null; }
export class Tray {
  constructor(deps: { channelId: Id; routes: Pick<Routes, 'putBlob' | 'deleteBlob'>; thumb: ThumbDeps | null; random(n: number): Uint8Array; onChange(entries: readonly TrayEntry[]): void });
  /** Refuses the whole call before reading anything: entries + files > 4 → E_ATTACHMENT_COUNT; any file > cap → E_ATTACHMENT_TOO_LARGE.
   *  Then per file, serially: reading (arrayBuffer) → preparing (key and nonce, sealBlob; for an image MIME the thumbnail, sealThumb,
   *  w/h) → uploading (putBlob) → ready; a failure sets failed with the code of the thrown DillaHttpError, AttachmentError or
   *  CoreError, else 'E_ATTACHMENT_FAILED'. Resolves with the new ids once each of its files is ready or failed (the slice shows
   *  the phases meanwhile). */
  add(files: readonly File[]): Promise<string[]>;
  /** deleteBlob when it was uploaded (a failure is swallowed: the reference expires after pending_ttl), then drops the entry. */
  discard(id: string): Promise<void>;
  /** The ready descriptors of `ids`, in order, removed from the tray, then onChange; any id not ready → Error('E_TRAY_NOT_READY')
   *  and nothing is removed. */
  take(ids: readonly string[]): AttachmentDescriptor[];
  entries(): readonly TrayEntry[];
}
// download.ts
/** getBlob(channel, blobId, d.size + 16) (null → AttachmentError E_ATTACHMENT_MISSING; E_BODY_TOO_LARGE → E_BLOB_OPEN) → openBlob
 *  → a Blob typed `mime` when RENDERABLE_IMAGE has it, else application/octet-stream. A descriptor whose size is over the cap
 *  → E_ATTACHMENT_TOO_LARGE before any request. */
export function fetchAttachment(routes: Pick<Routes, 'getBlob'>, channelId: Id, d: AttachmentDescriptor): Promise<Blob>;
/** openThumb, then isThumbnailBytes (else E_BLOB_OPEN); a Blob typed image/webp or image/jpeg by its magic. */
export function thumbnailBlob(d: AttachmentDescriptor): Promise<Blob>;
```

`sealThumb` over `MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT` throws `RangeError('E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT: thumbnail plaintext over 8176 bytes')` (a programming error: `makeThumbnail` never produces it; `AttachmentError['code']` gains nothing). `crypto.test.ts` reproduces every `attachment.json` case (`stored`, `blob_id`, open, thumb) and refuses every reject with its code, reading the committed file. **Mutation named (task 6):** `openBlob` without the hash comparison → the `E_BLOB_HASH` reject goes red.

**L-TS-33 mentions** (`src/state/mentions.ts`, exported from the package root; task 6; C23, Q20)

```ts
export type MentionTarget = 'everyone' | 'here' | string;          // a 32-hex user or role id
export type MentionPart = { kind: 'text'; text: string } | { kind: 'mention'; target: MentionTarget };
/** Splits on the literal tokens <@everyone>, <@here>, <@[0-9a-f]{32}>; adjacent text parts are merged; no other parsing. */
export function splitMentions(body: string): MentionPart[];
export interface MentionMember { userId: string; username: string; }
/** Rewrites `@word` → `<@userId>` where `@` starts the text or follows whitespace or one of ( [ { " ', word is the maximal run of
 *  [A-Za-z0-9._-] after it with trailing '.' removed, and word lower-cased equals a member's username; `@everyone`/`@here` →
 *  `<@everyone>`/`<@here>` only when `broadcast`; anything else is left as typed. */
export function encodeMentions(text: string, members: readonly MentionMember[], broadcast: boolean): string;
/** The partial `@word` that ends at `caret` (same boundary rule, 0..=32 run characters), else null. */
export function mentionQuery(text: string, caret: number): { start: number; query: string } | null;
/** mentions_me_with_roles' rule (L-CORE-35) over hex strings. */
export function mentionsMe(body: string, userHex: string, roleHexes: readonly string[]): boolean;
```

`state/badges.ts`'s `mentionsMe` (web-2a) is removed; `mentions.ts`'s `mentionsMe` is exported for the page (rendering `me` on pills) and is **not** used by the worker's notice rule, which reads the core's flag (L-TS-35; adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-07).

**L-TS-34 the engine's send hooks** (`src/sync/{engine,send,internals}.ts`; task 7; amends web-1 L-TS-07 rule 5)

```ts
export interface SyncDeps { /* web-2a */
  /** Called by drainOne before sendEncrypt for an outbox row with attachments, every attempt. Rejecting with a DillaHttpError
   *  404 fails the row with 'E_ATTACHMENT_MISSING'; any other rejection fails it with its code (the person may retry). */
  beforeSend(groupId: Id, row: OutboxRow): Promise<void>;
  /** Called by discardSend after sendDiscard with the row as the outbox held it. */
  onDiscarded(groupId: Id, row: OutboxRow): void;
}
export class SyncEngine { /* web-2a */ sendRequest(groupId: Id, request: SendRequest): Id; send(groupId: Id, text: string): Id; }   // web-2a's send(g, text) (engine.ts:346) stays, as sendRequest(g, {type 0…})
```

`discardSend` reads the row's attachments from `core.outbox` before `sendDiscard` and calls `deps.onDiscarded(groupId, row)` (a new required `SyncDeps` member; the controller deletes the references). The harness recorder and the controller's deps gain both members.

**L-TS-35 worker commands** (`src/worker/protocol.ts`; task 7; amends web-2a L-TS-23)

```ts
export type Command = /* web-2a, with `send` amended */
  | { m: 'send'; channelId: string; text: string; replyTo?: string | null; attachments?: readonly string[] }   // replyTo: msg id hex; attachments: tray ids
  | { m: 'editMessage'; channelId: string; msgId: string; text: string }
  | { m: 'deleteMessage'; channelId: string; msgId: string }
  | { m: 'react'; channelId: string; msgId: string; emoji: string; on: boolean }
  | { m: 'pin'; channelId: string; msgId: string; on: boolean }
  | { m: 'loadPins'; channelId: string }
  | { m: 'closePins'; channelId: string }
  | { m: 'attachFiles'; channelId: string; files: readonly File[] }
  | { m: 'discardAttachment'; channelId: string; trayId: string }
  | { m: 'openAttachment'; channelId: string; seq: string; index: number; thumb: boolean };
```

Results: `attachFiles` → `{ trayIds: string[] }`; `openAttachment` → `{ blob: Blob; name: string; mime: string }` (the one place a decrypted object crosses to the page; `name` is `safeName(name, '')` and the page shows `shell.attachment.unnamed` for `''`, so the worker holds no English); every other new command → `null`. `ACCEPTS.ready` gains the nine new methods. Error codes added: `E_ATTACHMENT_TOO_LARGE`, `E_ATTACHMENT_COUNT`, `E_ATTACHMENT_MISSING`, `E_BLOB_HASH`, `E_BLOB_OPEN`, `E_TRAY_NOT_READY`. Rules: `send` resolves `channelId` → its group as today; `attachments` → `tray.take(ids)`; `text` and `replyTo` and the descriptors → `sendRequest(g, { type: 0, … })` (the page has already run `encodeMentions`); `editMessage`/`deleteMessage`/`react`/`pin` → `sendRequest` with type 1 / 2 / 3 or 4 / 5 or 6 and `replyTo` = `msgId` (the core's refusals cross as `CoreError` codes); `emoji` must be 1..=32 UTF-8 bytes (`E_BAD_INPUT` otherwise). `beforeSend` = `confirmBlob(channel, blobId)` for each attachment of the row, in order. `onDiscarded` = `deleteBlob` for each (failures swallowed). **Purges:** `runPurges()` runs after every `onOutboxChanged` and after every gateway ready, single-flight (a request while one runs re-runs it once after): for each `core.purges()` row **whose group `core.groupRow(g)` reports in state 2** (a row of a group in any other state — the device was removed and has not rejoined — is skipped and kept for a later trigger, because the delivery service answers a non-member 404 and that 404 must not count as done; adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-08), `deleteGroupMessage(g, seq)` (204 or 404 both done), then `deleteBlob(channel, id)` for each blob id (204/404 done; a 403 is done too: the reference is not this user's), then `core.purgeDone(g, seq)`; any other failure stops this row until the next trigger. Residual (ruling 8): a device that never rejoins keeps its purge row and the instance keeps that ciphertext and those references until retention. **Notices:** a notice is a mention notice when `after > before && row.mention` (the core's flag, L-CORE-35); the worker never runs `mentionsMe` over a shown body (adjudicated, FACTS-SECURITY-07: an edit folded in the same apply must not raise a mention, ruling 4). **Roles:** whenever a `listMembers(c)` result holds the own user's row and its role ids differ from the last set applied for that community, `core.ownRolesSet(c, row.roleIds)`; the worker keeps the last applied hexes only to skip a redundant call. **Pins:** `loadPins` publishes `pins:<channel>` from `core.pins(g)` and keeps it fresh on every `onGroupChanged` of that group until `closePins` or `closeChannel`. **Tray:** one `Tray` per channel, `thumb` deps from `ControllerDeps.thumbs?: ThumbDeps | null` when given (a test seam, private to the package), else probed from the worker global (`createImageBitmap`, `new OffscreenCanvas(w, h)`; either missing → `null`), `random` = `crypto.getRandomValues`, published as `tray:<channel>` (without descriptors) on every change and after every successful `take`; `attachFiles` awaits `tray.add` and answers `{ trayIds }` (the controller's dispatch is concurrent, `controller.ts:304-309`, so a long upload blocks no other command); every tray is dropped **without requests** on a wipe (`forgetBrowser`, `signOutRevoke`) or a reset, its `tray:<channel>` published `[]` (the sessions are gone by then; the pending references expire after `blobs.pending_ttl`, L-HTTP-83). `openAttachment`: `core.attachmentGet(g, BigInt(seq), index)` → `thumb` and `d.thumb === null` → `AttachmentError('E_ATTACHMENT_MISSING', 'no thumbnail')`; `thumb ? thumbnailBlob(d) : fetchAttachment(routes, channel, d)`. **Mutations named:** confirm after `sendEncrypt` instead of before → the controller test asserting the request order `confirm` < `message` goes red; publish a tray entry with its descriptor → the test that serialises every published slice of a send-with-attachment run and searches it for the key bytes goes red.

**L-TS-36 slices** (`src/state/types.ts`; task 7; amends web-2a L-TS-24)

```ts
export interface ReplyRef { msgId: string; state: 'ok' | 'missing' | 'deleted'; senderUser: string | null; excerpt: string; seq: string | null; }
export interface ReactionSummary { emoji: string; count: number; mine: boolean; }
export interface AttachmentSummary { index: number; size: number; mime: string; name: string; w: number | null; h: number | null;
  thumb: boolean; kind: 'image' | 'file'; tooLarge: boolean; }   // kind 'image' iff RENDERABLE_IMAGE has mime; tooLarge iff size > cap
export interface PendingAction { msgId: string; type: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6; state: 'pending' | 'failed'; reason: string; }   // msgId: the fold row's OWN outbox msg id (retrySend/discardSend take it); the target is the item it hangs on
export interface MemberSummary { /* web-2a: userId, username, display, kind */ roleIds: string[]; }   // hex of member-row element 3, in order (adjudicated, INTERFACES-05)
export interface TimelineItem { /* web-2a fields */ seq: string | null; edited: boolean; reply: ReplyRef | null;
  reactions: ReactionSummary[]; pinned: boolean; attachments: AttachmentSummary[]; mention: boolean; actions: PendingAction[]; }
export interface PinnedItem { msgId: string; seq: string; senderUser: string | null; excerpt: string; pinnedBy: string; pinnedSeq: string; ts: number; }   // ts: the target's recv_ts, unix seconds
export interface TrayItem { id: string; name: string; size: number; mime: string; image: boolean; phase: 'reading' | 'preparing' | 'uploading' | 'ready' | 'failed'; reason: string; }
export type SliceName = /* web-2a */ | `pins:${string}` | `tray:${string}`;

```

`buildTimeline` maps the L-CORE-34 fields; an outbox row of type 0 is a pending/failed item with `attachments` from the outbox (no thumb, `seq` null); an outbox row of types 1–6 is **not** an item: it becomes a `PendingAction` on the item whose `msgId` equals its `replyTo` (dropped when that item is not loaded). `TIMELINE_PAGE` stays 100 and `hasEarlier` is `rows.length >= limit` over displayable rows only. Every `TimelineItem` construction site gains the fields: `packages/web/src/test/fixtures.ts` gains `timelineItem(over?: Partial<TimelineItem>): TimelineItem` and `packages/web/src/screens/Shell.test.tsx`'s `item()` spreads it (task 7; the stories in task 8/9). `publishMembers` fills `MemberSummary.roleIds` from each member row's role ids (hex, in order), and every `MemberSummary` literal in client-core and web tests gains `roleIds: []` (task 7, so its own `typecheck -w @dilla/web` stays green). `pins:<channel>` maps `PinRow.targetTs` to `ts: Number(targetTs)`.

**L-TS-37 page-side rules** (`packages/web`; task 9) — blob URLs: `useBlobUrl(blob: Blob | null)` mints with `URL.createObjectURL` in the page and revokes on change and unmount; a thumbnail is requested (`openAttachment { thumb: true }`) once per visible image card and kept for the item's life on screen; the lightbox requests the full file; saving calls `openAttachment { thumb: false }`, clicks an `<a download={name} href={url}>` it created, then revokes. Mentions: the composer runs `encodeMentions(value, members, kind !== 'dm')` at send and its byte counter measures the encoded text (`Composer.measure`); the mention list offers at most 8 members whose username or display name starts with the query (case-insensitive; username prefix first), then `everyone` in channels (no `here` option: the client has no presence, ruling 29 as amended; a typed `@here` is still encoded and counts as everyone); picking inserts `@username ` (or `@everyone `). Bodies render through `splitMentions`: a user id names the member's display or username (`@`-prefixed), an unknown id `shell.message.mentionUnknown` with its first 8 hex, a role `shell.message.mentionRole`; `me` is set for the own user, own roles, `everyone` and `here`. Notifications (web-2a card 48): `notify.ts` renders the body through the same substitution, never a raw token. The delete action always opens the delete dialog first.
