```ts
// L-UI-50 native <dialog> filling the viewport: the image contained, the label, save and close buttons, previous/next when given;
//          Escape → onClose; ArrowLeft/ArrowRight → previous/next; focus to the close button on open
export interface LightboxProps { open: boolean; label: string; src: string | null; alt: string; closeLabel: string; onClose(): void;
  saveLabel: string; onSave(): void; previous?: { label: string; onPrevious(): void }; next?: { label: string; onNext(): void }; }
// L-UI-51 an aria-hidden overlay over the main pane while files are dragged over it (the page announces through its status region)
export interface DropOverlayProps { active: boolean; title: string; body: string; }
// L-UI-52 MessageLog (amends web-1): `onKeyDown` on the log for the roving rows; role=log, aria-live="polite" and
//          aria-relevant="additions" (SLICE-UX-08). The log's own tabIndex is -1 while a row inside holds tabindex="0" and 0
//          otherwise, set by a layout effect after every render (one tab stop; the log stays programmatically focusable, so
//          web-1's focusLog() and Shell's remount hand-over keep working; axe's scrollable-region-focusable holds because the
//          active row is focusable). A MessageLog test asserts aria-relevant="additions" and both tabIndex states.
export interface MessageLogProps { /* web-1 */ onKeyDown?(e: React.KeyboardEvent): void; }
// L-UI-53 Composer (amends web-1): an attach button before the textarea, a `top` slot above (reply chip, tray, mention list),
//          `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant` ONLY while
//          `combobox.expanded` is true (closed: the web-1 textbox role and name); `combobox.onKey` is called for the five keys
//          whenever `combobox` is given, expanded or not (true consumes the key); `canSendEmpty` lets submit() send a blank value
//          (the page passes it while the tray holds at least one entry; the page itself refuses a send while an entry is not
//          ready); `measure` for the budget, `onArrowUpEmpty` for editing the last own message, `onPasteFiles` for pasted files
export interface ComposerProps { /* web-1 */ attachLabel?: string; onAttach?(): void; top?: React.ReactNode; measure?(v: string): number;
  canSendEmpty?: boolean;
  combobox?: { expanded: boolean; controls: string; activeDescendant: string | null; onKey(key: 'ArrowUp' | 'ArrowDown' | 'Enter' | 'Tab' | 'Escape'): boolean };
  onCaret?(caret: number): void; onArrowUpEmpty?(): void; onPasteFiles?(files: File[]): void; textareaRef?: React.Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>; }
// L-UI-54 ChannelHeader (amends web-2a L-UI-30): `actions?: React.ReactNode` rendered after the topic (the pins button)
export interface ChannelHeaderProps { /* web-2a */ actions?: React.ReactNode; }
```

DOM contract the screens and the e2e rely on: each message row carries `data-seq` (or nothing for a pending item), `data-msg-id`, `data-edited="true"` when edited, `data-pinned="true"` when pinned, `data-mention="true"` when it mentions the viewer, and `data-state`; the toolbar is `role="toolbar"` named `shell.message.toolbar`, its buttons named by their labels; a reaction chip is `button[aria-pressed]` named `{name}, {count}` with `data-emoji`; a row carries `data-flash="true"` while it flashes; the reply line is a `button` inside `.d-message-row__reply` whose accessible name is its visible text (`{author} {excerpt}`) and whose description holds `shell.message.replyLabel`/`.replyMissing`/`.replyDeleted` and `shell.message.replyJump` (the e2e locates it by role `button` inside `.d-message-row__reply`); the editor is a `textarea` named `shell.edit.label`; the mention list is `role="listbox"` named `shell.composer.mentions` with `role="option"` items, and the composer textarea is `role="combobox"` only while it is open; the emoji grid is a `role="dialog"` named `shell.emoji.label` outside `role="log"`; the pins dialog is a `<dialog>` named by its title (`Dialog`'s `<h2>`, `packages/ui/src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx:33`); a tray entry is an `<li>` with `data-phase` (from `step`); an image card's `<img>` has `alt` = the shown name and `data-thumb="ready"` once its `src` is set; a file card's save button is named `shell.attachment.save`; the lightbox is a `<dialog>` with an `<img>` whose `alt` is the name.

### L-E2E — test peers and specs

**L-E2E-20 `dilla-testkit web-driver` verbs** (`testkit/src/web_driver.rs`; task 5; the JSON-lines framing of web-1 L-E2E-01)

| op | request fields | answer fields | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `send` (changed) | web-2a's `body`, `channel_id`; `type` (optional uint 0..=6, default 0), `reply_to` (optional 32-hex msg id; required for 1..=6) | `seq`, `msg_id` (32-hex) | frames the envelope with that type and `reply_to` (body rules of 04: `""` for 2/5/6) |
| `sync` (changed) | as web-2a | each `received` row gains `msg_id`, `type`, `reply_to` (hex or null), `deleted` (bool: a served `deleted = 1` or op 21), `attachments: [{ index, blob_id, size, mime, name, thumb: bool }]` | as web-2a; a deleted row appears with `body ""`; a row deleted before the peer ever held it answers `msg_id`, `type`, `reply_to`, `sender_user`, `sender_device` and `tier` as `null` (every TypeScript type of these fields — task 7's `PeerRow`, task 10's `PeerReceived` — is `string \| null` / `number \| null`; INTERFACES-11) |
| `delete` | `msg_id`, `seq` (the peer's own message), `channel_id` (optional) | `seq` (the type-2 row) | sends type 2 with `reply_to = msg_id`, then `DELETE /v1/groups/{g}/messages/{seq}`, then `DELETE` of each attachment reference that message carried |
| `attach` | `channel_id` (optional), `name`, `mime`, `body` (optional, default `""`), either `bytes_hex` (decoded ≤ 1 048 576 bytes) or `size` (1..=26214400) with `seed` (uint: plaintext byte i = SHA-256(seed ‖ i/32 as u64 BE)[i mod 32]), optional `w`, `h`, `thumb_hex` (decoded ≤ 8176 bytes) | `seq`, `msg_id`, `blob_id` (64-hex), `sha256` (64-hex of the plaintext) | a fresh key and nonce per `attach`: the driver's counter goes up by one, `key = SHA-256("dilla-testkit attachment key" ‖ driver seed u64 BE ‖ counter u64 BE)` and `nonce = SHA-256("dilla-testkit attachment nonce" ‖ driver seed u64 BE ‖ counter u64 BE)[0..12]` (task 5's drafted `attachment_material`) — the testkit has no OS-entropy RNG and no crate may be added (peer-client 6); a test peer needs a fresh key per blob, not unpredictability — then `seal_blob`, `PUT` octet-stream, `POST …/confirm`, `seal_thumb` when given, then a type-0 envelope with the one attachment |
| `fetch_attachment` | `channel_id` (optional), `seq`, `index` | `sha256`, `size`, `mime`, `name`, `thumb_sha256` (64-hex or null) | `GET` (the body read with ureq's `into_with_config().limit(104_857_600)`, dillad's `blobs.max_blob_bytes` default — `read_to_vec`'s 10 MiB default, `ureq-3.4.2/src/body/mod.rs:30`, would refuse a 25 MiB file; TESTS-01), `open_blob` (`E_BLOB_HASH`/`E_BLOB_OPEN` become the error string `scenario: E_BLOB_…`), `open_thumb` when present |
| `blob_status` | `channel_id` (optional), `blob_id` | `status` (200 or 404) | the HTTP status of a `GET` of that reference |

**L-E2E-21 `e2e/web/conversation.spec.ts`** (task 10; projects `chromium-web`, `firefox-web`; a peer with `setup`, browser A signs up through onboarding with the instance invite and joins the peer's community with the peer's code (`signUp(page, instanceInvite(), …)` then `joinCommunity`, as `e2e/web/badges.spec.ts:35-36`; code wins, web-e2e 13) and opens the channel; browser B is a second persistent context, `second.open()`, that signs up as a second user with the same instance invite and joins the same way): (1) **"edit, reply, react, pin and delete between the browser and the peer"** — A sends; the peer `sync`s it; A edits it in place (`ArrowUp` from the empty composer, type, `Enter`) → the peer receives type 1 with `reply_to` = A's msg id; the peer sends, then edits its message → A's row shows the new body and `data-edited="true"`; A replies to the peer's message → the peer receives type 0 with `reply_to`, and A's reply line (the `button` inside `.d-message-row__reply`) names the peer and jumps (the target row gets `data-flash="true"`); the peer reacts `👍` → A shows the chip `thumbs up, 1` not pressed; A toggles it → `thumbs up, 2` pressed, the peer receives type 3; A pins the peer's message → the pins dialog lists it `pinned by <A>`, and the peer receives type 5; the dialog's `unpin` → A's row loses `data-pinned` and the peer receives type 6; A deletes its own message through the dialog → the peer receives type 2 and, on its next `sync`, the target row `deleted: true`; the peer deletes its own message (`peer.deleteMessage`) → A's row of that msg id reaches `data-state="deleted"` and no longer shows its text. (2) **"an edit or a delete by someone else changes nothing"** — the peer sends `send {type 1, reply_to: A's msg id}`, then `send {type 2, reply_to: A's msg id}`, then a plain message; A shows the plain message (the positive control) and A's own row unchanged: `data-state="ok"`, its text, no `data-edited` (attacker statement: only the author's own type 1/2 folds, L-CORE-33). (3) **"mentions"** — A first opens channel 2; in B's composer (channel 1) `@` + the first letters of A's username opens the list; `Enter` inserts `@<username> `; B sends; the peer `sync` receives `<@<A hex>>`; A's channel-1 row in the channel list shows `data-mentions="1"` (the chain autocomplete → `encodeMentions` → A's core flag → A's badge, SLICE-UX-11); A opens channel 1 and that row has `data-mention="true"`, its body shows `@<A's name>` and never `<@`; the peer sends `<@<B hex>> look` while B sits in another channel of the server (`setup` with `channels: 2`) → B's row of the first channel shows `data-mentions="1"` (web-2a's badge), and opening it shows the row with `data-mention="true"`. (4) **"images and files go both ways"** — A attaches a 320×240 PNG drawn in the page by canvas and a 70 000-byte file through the hidden input; the tray reaches `ready` for both; A sends; the peer's `fetch_attachment` answers the same `sha256` A computed in the page for each and a `thumb_sha256` for the image; the peer `attach`es a PNG (bytes drawn by canvas in the page and passed as hex) with a WebP thumbnail (also drawn there) and a file of `size 70000, seed 7` → A shows an image card whose `img` reaches `data-thumb="ready"` with `naturalWidth > 0`, opens the lightbox (its image loads), and saves the file (a Playwright `download` whose bytes hash to the peer's `sha256`); A deletes its attachment message → the peer's `blob_status` of both blobs is 404. (5) **"a 25 MB file goes through and one byte more is refused"** — a 26 214 400-byte file reaches `ready` and the peer's `fetch_attachment` matches it; a 26 214 401-byte file is refused at the tray with `shell.tray.tooLarge` and no upload request is made (the PUT count is read from `context.on('request')`; step 3 first runs this test alone on both projects and records whether Firefox reports the dedicated worker's fetches there; if it does not, the two PUT-count assertions run only when `browserName === 'chromium'`, while the refusal, the alert, the absent tray entry and the 10-byte positive control run on both, and the "refused before any request" property rests on task 6's `Tray` unit test and its mutation (d) — TESTS-08). (6) **"B sees what A makes"** — A edits, reacts and pins; B's view shows the edited body, the chip and `data-pinned="true"`; A attaches the canvas PNG and a 70 000-byte file and sends; B's row shows the image card at `data-thumb="ready"` with `naturalWidth > 0` (a thumbnail one browser's worker encoded, rendered by another user's page under the served CSP), B opens the lightbox (its image loads), and B saves the file (a Playwright `download` whose bytes hash to the SHA-256 A computed in the page) (SLICE-UX-06, SLICE-UX-12). Axe with `target-size` runs on the conversation with the toolbar open, the emoji grid, the pins dialog, the lightbox and the tray. Every spec closes both contexts and the driver in `finally`; the canvas-drawn images are produced at test time (no binary fixture). **Mutations named (task 10):** make the browser's fold accept an edit from any user (ModelCore is not involved: change `fold.rs` step 3 in a scratch build used only for the red run) → test 2 goes red; seal blobs with an empty AAD in `crypto.ts` → test 4's peer `fetch_attachment` fails `E_BLOB_OPEN`.

## Tasks

Eleven tasks in six drafting units. Every task ends with the tree green under its own gates and one commit (task 11 may need more). "Mutation" names the change that must turn the task's critical assertion red (lesson a). The Rust core critical path runs first (1–3); dillad (4) is independent of 1–3 and may be drafted in parallel; the native peer and the client port (5–6); the worker integration and the components (7–8); the web conversation and the browser proof (9–10); CI and docs close (11). Block boundaries (full suites) after tasks 4, 7 and 10.

No spike task: the one fact the authorities left unmeasured, WebCrypto's peak memory at 25 MiB (Q16 "until measured"), does not decide any later task — the cap is fixed by ruling and gap-G5 measured the 100 MiB case (+460–650 MiB peak) — so task 10 proves the 25 MiB round trip as a mechanism in both engines instead (ruling 13).

Departures acted on here are recorded where ruled: DEV-W2-01 (C23 written), DEV-W2-02 (author-only delete), DEV-W2-06 (`reply_to` required), DEV-W2-08 (pins and `@everyone` from any member, Q20), DEV-W2-09 (member-only delete), DEV-W2-35 (no client attachment cache; the server tables unchanged), DEV-W2-36 (`pending_ttl` read at last; `limits.max_attachment_bytes` stays dead and is left for a config-cleanup card), DEV-W2-37 (no preview generation; received previews not rendered yet, Deferred), DEV-W2-38 (the comment fixed), DEV-W2-39 (the drop copy without encryption words), DEV-W2-40 (references deleted with their message), DEV-W2-41 (the AEAD with vectors), DEV-W2-42 (`img-src 'self' blob:` only), DEV-W2-60 (attachment-only messages render their cards).

## Deferred to web-2b / web-2c / web-3

(This plan is web-2b: the table lists what it leaves to web-2c, web-3 and later cards.)

Nothing in this list is drafted into a web-2b task. Where the slice meets one of these, it shows what the right-hand column says.

| left out | what web-2b does instead |
|---|---|
| Leaf validation (F11), TOFU pins, safety numbers, Settings → Privacy, the device-list ingest of other users (web-2c) | Unchanged from web-2a: the folds trust the MLS credential's `user_id`, which the delivery service's invariant 4 already binds to a listed device |
| Search over folded bodies, the palette, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+/ (web-2c; Q21) | None; the schema keeps `edit_body` so web-2c's FTS triggers index the shown body |
| Typing indicators (web-2c, Q22), presence | None |
| Settings surface, Diagnostics, the cannot-read copy (web-2c) | Cannot-read rows keep the raw code |
| Tab hand-over (web-2c) | A second tab still waits; a `blob:` URL never outlives its page anyway |
| Voice, video, audio and video attachments playing inline (web-3; `media-src blob:` then) | Audio and video files are file cards to save |
| Threads, the thread panel, "reply in thread" (F6) | `thread_id` stays null on send and is ignored on receipt |
| Quote reply, forward, "mark unread from here", "save message", "copy link to message", the right-click menu | The toolbar's five actions only |
| Receipt permission checks for pins and `@everyone`/`@here`; role names; the role/overwrite read routes (Q20) | Pins and broadcast mentions from any current member; a role mention shows as `@role` and counts only for roles learned from a loaded member page (no backfill) |
| Rendering received link previews (F7: receivers may render them) | A preview is not shown; the URL is in the body as text |
| Markdown, code blocks, autolinks, custom emoji, a free emoji picker, emoji in the composer | Plain text bodies; reactions from the fixed 32 |
| Edit history | Only the latest edit is shown, marked `edited` |
| Moderator deletion of others' E2EE messages (a signed moderation event, 09) | The author only |
| Attachments over 25 MiB in a browser; chunked or streamed AES-GCM; upload byte progress (fetch has none) | Refused at the tray; received ones show `shell.attachment.tooLarge`; the tray shows phases, not percentages |
| A decrypted attachment cache (Q17: none) | Each open downloads and opens again; thumbnails come from the envelope |
| Re-encoding or stripping image metadata before sending | The file is sent as chosen; only the thumbnail is newly encoded |
| Archive (kind 2) carrying folds; `06:77-78`'s merge rule | No archive writer exists in browsers (web-2a) |
| Cross-device read sync, notifications for edits or reactions | Badges and notices count type-0 messages only; an edit never notifies |
| `limits.max_attachment_bytes` (dead config) and its removal | Untouched |
| Readable (`mode 1`) channels (Q07) | Still `unsupported` in the client; dillad's readable receiver gets the `04` rules |

## Rulings made by the architect

Each is a decision the authorities left open. Form: what — why — what it costs if wrong.

1. **Ruling: the attachment element gains a ninth element, `name` (tstr ≤ 255 bytes), in the same `04` edit as the AEAD.** — A file card and a saved file need a name, protocol/04's eight elements carry none, and no client has shipped an attachment; putting the name inside the sealed blob would make `size` and the thumbnail rules about a container instead of the file. — The envelope vectors, the Rust and Go decoders and the generator change once; a later reader of old envelopes would need an 8-element branch, which nobody has written.
2. **Ruling: types 1–6 require `reply_to` and carry no attachments or previews; the core refuses them on decode, dillad's readable receiver likewise.** — Q18 makes `reply_to` required; an edit "replaces the body" (04:36), so files on a fold have no meaning to fold, and refusing them keeps one shape per type. — An edit cannot change a message's files; a person deletes and sends again.
3. **Ruling: the fold is a set of derived tables recomputed per target from the stored rows (`refold`), decided by the highest group `seq` per rule, with target resolution by the earliest type-0 row carrying the msg id.** — Every fold row is stored anyway (web-1), so recomputing from rows is idempotent, order-independent across catch-up, adoption and confirm paths, makes "parked folds" free (a later target insert refolds), and is exactly what a v2 store's backfill needs; the earliest-row rule closes card 20's duplicate msg id without a new table. — (Amended by the adjudication, FACTS-SECURITY-02.) The drafted whole-target recompute was O(n²) per refold and O(n³) per catch-up, which any member within the message meter (1/s, burst 20 per device, `defaults.go:52`; up to 8 devices) could turn against every other member's worker. A refold is now scoped by the row that caused it (`FoldScope`, L-CORE-33) and every statement is an index search proven by `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, so an insert costs a constant number of index searches; the view shows at most 20 distinct reactions per message. Cost if wrong: three indexes on `app_messages` (a few bytes per fold row) and a 21st distinct emoji not shown.
4. **Ruling: an edit never raises or clears a mention and never notifies.** — Q09's notices are for new messages; an edit that pings is a known abuse in chat apps, and the flag is set once at apply. — Someone who adds a mention by editing must send a new message to reach the person.
5. **Ruling: a delete (by type 2 from the author, or the delivery service's tombstone) also blanks the bodies of the target's edit rows and drops its reactions and pins.** — "A delete wins" (06:77-78) and the person expects the words gone from every device that honours it, including earlier versions held as edit rows — also on a device that never held the target because the delivery service's tombstone reached it first (L-CORE-33 step 1, adjudicated FACTS-SECURITY-03). — Nothing; reactions on a deleted message have no anchor to show.
6. **Ruling: Q17's `pending_ttl` is implemented as an unconfirmed reference that its uploader confirms through `POST …/blobs/{blob_id}/confirm` before sending the message; the sweeper drops unconfirmed references older than `pending_ttl`.** — The literal reading ("a reference older than 24 h with a single reference from its uploader") describes every delivered attachment (each channel reference has exactly one row, its uploader's, `008_blobs.sql:19-30`), so it would delete every image after a day; the server cannot see messages (`blobs.go` writes the reference at PUT time with an empty mime), so only the uploader can say an upload is in use. Existing references migrate as confirmed. — One route, one column and one migration on both engines; a tab that dies between the confirm and the send leaves a confirmed orphan that retention collects, as before. **This departs from the controller's Q17 text** (adjudication, FACTS-SECURITY-11): it is recorded here as **DEV-W2b-01 (pending the controller's ratification; to be copied into `facts/deviations.md` by the controller, which this plan may not edit)**: "Q17's `pending_ttl` reads 'a reference older than 24 h with a single reference from its uploader'; taken literally it would delete every delivered attachment after a day, so web-2b implements it as an unconfirmed reference its uploader confirms through `POST …/blobs/{blob_id}/confirm` before sending; every client that uploads for any reason confirms (09 § Blobs)". Every non-browser client of this tree that uploads (the testkit's `attach`) confirms.
7. **Ruling: files upload when attached (the tray), are confirmed before every `send_encrypt` attempt of the row that names them, and the tray lives in worker memory only.** — Mesh's tray shows upload progress before send; confirming from the outbox row makes the confirm durable across reloads without a new table; an abandoned tray costs nothing after `pending_ttl`. — A reload loses unsent tray items (the person attaches again).
8. **Ruling: the delete's server work (the delivery-service `DELETE` and the reference deletes) is recorded by the core as an `app_purges` row on the sending device's own fold of its own type 2, and carried out by the worker after confirm and at every ready.** — Q19 orders three steps across two route families; a durable record survives a reload between them, and only the device that sent the delete holds the duty (another device of the same user would only repeat it). — A purge that keeps failing retries at every ready; a 403 or 404 counts as done, but only while the group is in state 2 (a removed device's 404 is the membership refusal, not completion; adjudicated FACTS-SECURITY-08); a device that never rejoins leaves the ciphertext and references to retention.
9. **Ruling: `timeline` returns displayable rows only (type 0 or NULL).** — web-1's `buildTimeline` hid fold rows after they had taken page slots (`derive.ts:19-20`), so a busy reaction channel could page out its messages; the core now does the filtering where the page size is applied. — The notice read sees no fold rows, which is the rule anyway.
10. **Ruling: the fold rules get a second parity fixture, `fold_parity.json`, asserting the timeline view; `group_apply_parity.json` stays at eight cases.** — Q18 asks for fixture cases by ruling; the folds change no `group_apply` result, so the existing fixture would test nothing new, while a view fixture pins the semantics both implementations must share. — Two runners per language.
11. **Ruling: `send_prepare` takes no mention list; mentions travel only in the body (C23 syntax), the page turns a typed or picked `@username` of a known member into `<@hex>` at send and renders tokens as names.** — The receiver must parse bodies anyway (C23), and a separate list would be a second source that can disagree with the body. — A person who writes `@bob` for a non-member gets plain text; usernames are unique and ASCII (`internal/auth/handle.go:65-80`), so matching is exact.
12. **Ruling: role mentions count through `own_roles_set`, fed by the worker from any loaded member page that holds the own user's row; rows applied earlier are not re-flagged.** — Q20 rules that role mentions match own role ids, the core counts mentions at apply, and the own role ids reach the client only on member rows (`09:216`); fetching every community's member list at ready to find one row would cost a read per page per community. — A role mention in a community whose member list was never opened on this device does not badge until it is.
13. **Ruling: no spike task; the 25 MiB browser cap stands (Q16) and task 10 proves a 25 MiB round trip and the refusal of one byte more in Chromium and Firefox.** — gap-G5 measured 100 MiB (peak +460–650 MiB), a quarter of that is well inside a desktop worker, and a memory figure would not change any task; the mechanism test is what lesson c allows. — If a low-memory device fails at 25 MiB, the cap constant changes in one place (`BROWSER_ATTACHMENT_CAP`) and in three strings.
14. **Ruling: attachment keys never leave the worker: slices carry summaries, `attachment_get` reads descriptors from the stored envelope on demand, the tray keeps descriptors in memory, and only `openAttachment` returns a decrypted `Blob` to the page, which mints and revokes `blob:` URLs (G5).** — The Global Constraint "no key in a slice or postMessage", and a worker-minted URL dies with the worker. — A thumbnail costs one command round trip per card.
15. **Ruling: images render only for `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`, `image/gif`; a thumbnail renders only with a WebP or JPEG signature; everything else is a file to save.** — The `mime` is the sender's claim; an allowlist keeps SVG and unknown types out of `<img>` and the lightbox. — An AVIF or HEIC photo is a file card until the list grows.
16. **Ruling: the thumbnail is encoded WebP at falling qualities and sizes (320, 240, 160, 120 px), then JPEG, checking the returned `Blob.type` (the silent PNG fallback, X2), and is omitted when nothing fits 8 176 bytes.** — Q17's format and bound, made deterministic enough to test with injected encoders. — A very detailed image may ship without a thumbnail and shows a neutral box until opened.
17. **Ruling: the tray shows phases (`reading`, `preparing`, `uploading`, `ready`, `failed`), not byte progress.** — `fetch` has no upload progress and Firefox lacks request streams; the F10 copy rule keeps "encrypting/sealed" out of the chrome. — Large uploads show only "uploading" until done.
18. **Ruling: ABI 6 changes `send_prepare` in place to take the CBOR request, rather than adding a second export.** — One send path keeps one set of checks; no client outside this tree calls the facade. — The facade spike and `core-handle.spec.ts` change with it (task 3).
19. **Ruling: each core shape change carries its TypeScript decoder in the same task (task 2 the timeline row, task 3 the ABI-6 port), with typed stand-ins in the doubles until task 6's full mirror.** — `wrapCore` decodes exact element counts (`cbor/index.ts:156-161`), so a core task that changed a row alone would break the core-worker and web suites until task 6; the fix is small next to a red block. — Tasks 2 and 3 run TS and browser gates.
20. **Ruling: the delivery-service delete answers a non-member `404 E_NOT_FOUND` (what `requireMember` answers) and checks it before the uploader rule.** — Every member-only group route answers so, to keep group existence unprobeable (`registry.go:502-511`); the uploader is a member by construction, so honest deletes are unaffected. — A removed device cannot delete its old messages; another of its user's member devices can.
21. **Ruling: the conversation's keyboard model is a roving active row in the log with only the active row's controls tabbable, and `ArrowUp` in an empty composer edits the last own message.** — Mesh's hover toolbar must be reachable without a mouse, a tab stop per chip would make the log untraversable, and `ArrowUp` is not a character key (2.1.4; Q14 forbids single-character keys only). — Screen-reader users move by arrow keys inside the log, which is the log pattern's own convention.
22. **Ruling: the reaction set is Mesh's 32 emoji (`chat-app.jsx:389-393`) in a grid, each with a name string; received reactions outside the set are shown and named by themselves.** — No emoji library may be added (C24 and the pin table), and the set is the design authority's. — Some people want more emoji; a picker card can grow the set.
23. **Ruling: a pin is visible to and removable by anyone in the conversation, and the pins dialog names who pinned.** — Q20 defers the permission check; naming the pinner is what keeps an unchecked pin accountable. — A member can unpin something a moderator pinned until web-2c's permissions land.
24. **Ruling: deleting always asks in a dialog; there is no undo and no shift-click shortcut.** — A delete reaches every device and the instance's copy; a confirm is the only proportionate guard, and a modifier shortcut would be a new shortcut Q14 does not name. — One extra click per delete.
25. **Ruling: the wasi guest is rebuilt locally and its vectors golden regenerated by task 1, without touching `core/dilla-core-wasi` or the wasi ABI.** — The guest embeds `run_all` (`exports.rs:87`), CI's Go jobs download a fresh guest, and `vectors_suites.golden` pins every case name, so the new suite must appear there in the same commit. — Each later Go task rebuilds the git-ignored guest before its first Go test.
26. **Ruling: the server's sweep reason for pending references is `"pending"` on the existing `blob_refs_expired` counter.** — One metric for every dropped reference with a reason label is the existing pattern (`metrics.go:246-253`). — None.
27. **Ruling: facts corrected by the code while writing this head.** `interfaces.md` A7's size (3,152,470 B, headroom 247,530 B) is web-1's: at `89ea4e0` the release wasm is 3,218,733 B (web-2a card 34). The sweeper is built in `cmd/dillad/serve.go:228`, not `internal/dillad/server.go`. `facts-attachments.md` U6 and U7 are settled by gap-G5 (worker `blob:` URLs resolve in the page under `img-src blob:` and die with the worker; downloads need no CSP change). `interfaces.md` A1's "no thumb format" is settled by Q17 and ruling 16. `facts-messages.md` §2's "per user or per device" is settled per user (Q18) and the same lens's unknown 9 (a fold whose target is not held) by ruling 3. The readable route already required `reply_to` for edits and deletes (`readable.go:479-480`), so the 09 edit widens an existing rule rather than adding one. `interfaces.md` A12 counts four Go pins of the CSP; the browser suite pins it a fifth time (`e2e/web/csp-axe.spec.ts:10`), which task 4 owns.
28. **Ruling: emoji reactions are toggled by the page from `mine` (type 3 when not mine, type 4 when mine); the worker does not de-duplicate.** — The fold makes a repeated add or remove harmless (the highest `seq` decides), so the page's view is enough. — Two quick clicks may send an add and a remove that both fold; the result is still the last click.
29. **Ruling: `@here` means everyone in the conversation, as `@everyone` does, until presence exists; the mention list does not offer it.** — The client has no presence (F5 later), and C23 adopts the readable syntax whose server counts both alike. (Amended by the adjudication, SLICE-UX-15: a list entry "everyone here now" would promise presence the client lacks, against the copy rule; the entry and `shell.composer.mentionHere` are dropped, a typed `@here` is still encoded and a received `<@here>` still renders as `@here`.) — When presence lands, a list entry and its string come back with it.
30. **Ruling: the composer converts typed `@everyone`/`@here` only in community channels, never in DMs.** — In a DM every participant is already addressed, and a broadcast token there would only add a mention badge to each message. — None.

### Rulings made in adjudication (2026-10-07; the review of tasks 1–11; `adjudication.md` lists every finding)

31. **Ruling: the v2→v3 backfill reads `reply_to` by a structural CBOR walk, never by `Envelope::decode`, and the timeline answers `[]` attachments for a stored envelope the v3 decoder refuses.** — web-2a stored envelopes the v3 decoder refuses and any member can send them today; a decode in the migration would let one message lock a person out of their store forever (lesson e, the web-1 rejoin-floor class). — A legacy fold row with a null `reply_to` folds onto nothing, which is what its sender asked for.
32. **Ruling: a refold is scoped by the row that caused it (`FoldScope`), every fold statement is an index search, and the timeline shows at most 20 distinct reactions per message (highest count first, displayed in first-reacted order).** — Ruling 3's whole-target recompute let any member make every other member's catch-up cubic; bounding the work and the chips removes the lever without changing a single fold result. — Three indexes; a 21st distinct emoji is not displayed.
33. **Ruling: when the target is not held, the author's own type-2 row blanks the author's own type-1 rows naming it.** — A device offline across the send and the delivery service's tombstone otherwise keeps the deleted words in plaintext in its store (and in web-2c's search index later). — Nothing an honest party relies on: only a user's own words are blanked, and only by that user's own delete.
34. **Ruling: the notice's mention is the core's `mention` flag; the worker never re-derives it from a body.** — The shown body may hold an edit folded in the same apply, and ruling 4 says an edit never raises a mention; one decision in one place. — None.
35. **Ruling: `runPurges` acts only on groups in state 2.** — The delivery service answers a non-member 404, which would otherwise erase a removed device's delete duty. — A purge waits for a rejoin; a device that never rejoins leaves the ciphertext to retention.
36. **Ruling: the pins row carries the target's `recv_ts` (a seventh element) and `PinnedItem.ts`.** — L-UI-47 needs a time for every pin, not only for pins whose target is on the loaded page. — One element in four decoders (Rust test, `wrapCore`, `ModelCore`, the slice).
37. **Ruling: one shape per crossing gap: the test decoders are task 2's (`(emoji, count, mine 0|1)`, `pinned: u64`, `has_thumb: u64`); the tray item field is `step`; the composer flag is `canSendEmpty`; the combobox role follows `expanded` while `onKey` always runs; `MemberSummary.roleIds` is published by task 7; `FakeServer.groupDelete` over `ModelDs.deleteAs`; `refold` is `pub(super)`; `wrapCore.ownRolesSet`'s detail is the core's.** — Each was drafted two ways by two units; the producer that lands first wins unless it breaks a contract. — Renames in the consuming task only.
38. **Ruling: `getBlob` takes `maxBytes` and the transport bounds a body with `maxBodyBytes`; `fetchAttachment` passes `size + 16`.** — A faulty or hostile instance could make the worker buffer an unbounded body for a 25 MiB descriptor. — One optional request field and a chunked read in `client.ts`.
39. **Ruling: the reply line's button is named by its visible text and described by its state and jump labels; the toolbar shows on hover, focus-within and on the active row only while focus is in the log, and in flow in the narrow shell; the log is `aria-relevant="additions"` and the emoji grid lives outside it.** — WCAG 2.5.3 (level A), flow 04's own wireframes, and announcements that do not read 32 emoji names. — A sighted keyboard user sees the toolbar only once in the log, which is where its keys work.
40. **Ruling: the wasm budget of task 1 is kept by shrinking `attachment.json` case 4 to 300 bytes and deriving four blob rejects from case 2; the large-file round trip is a native unit test.** — The vector JSON is embedded in the browser wasm; the ledger's file alone would have exceeded the budget. — None for cross-implementation coverage (AES-GCM's counter is position-independent and case 3 spans 63 blocks).
41. **Ruling: the native peer's attachment key and nonce are SHA-256-derived per `attach` from the driver's seed and a counter.** — The testkit has no OS RNG and no crate may be added; a test peer needs fresh keys, not secret ones. — None outside tests.
42. **Ruling: no task is added; the eleven tasks stand.** — Every finding fits the task that owns its files; new work (the query-plan test, the unheld-delete branch, the body bound, the extra e2e steps) lands in tasks 2, 6, 7 and 10 under their existing gates. — Tasks 2 and 10 grow by about a tenth.

    ```rust
    pub const AAD_THUMB: &[u8] = b"dilla thumb v1";
    pub const TAG_LEN: usize = 16;
    /// 8 192 (the envelope's thumb bound, on the sealed bytes) minus the tag.
    pub const MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT: usize = 8_176;
    /// nonce with byte 11 XOR 0x01.
    pub fn thumb_nonce(nonce: &[u8; 12]) -> [u8; 12];
    /// SHA-256 of the stored bytes.
    pub fn blob_id(stored: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32];
    /// AES-256-GCM(key, nonce, aad = AAD_BLOB) over the file; returns ct ‖ tag (plaintext length + 16 bytes).
    pub fn seal_blob(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], plaintext: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>;
    /// Order: blob_id(stored) != blob_id → E_BLOB_HASH; stored shorter than TAG_LEN or the AEAD fails → E_BLOB_OPEN;
    /// plaintext length != size → E_BLOB_OPEN. Returns the plaintext.
    pub fn open_blob(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], blob_id: &[u8; 32], size: u64, stored: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ProtocolError>;
    /// AES-256-GCM(key, thumb_nonce(nonce), aad = AAD_THUMB); plaintext over MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT → E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT.
    pub fn seal_thumb(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ProtocolError>;
    /// The AEAD fails or thumb is shorter than TAG_LEN → E_BLOB_OPEN.
    pub fn open_thumb(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], thumb: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ProtocolError>;
    ```

**Requirements:**
1. `Attachment` carries `name: String` as its ninth field and ninth wire element (`tstr`); `write` emits 9 elements; `read` requires exactly 9 (`d.array(9)`, so an 8- or 10-element attachment is `E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`) and refuses `name` over `MAX_NAME` bytes while reading (`E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT`, as `mime` at `:278-280`) (L-CORE-30; ruling 1).
2. `validate`, after every existing check and in this order: any attachment `name.len() > MAX_NAME` → `EnvelopeLimit`; when `kind != Message`: `reply_to.is_none()` → `EnvelopeShape`; `!attachments.is_empty() || !previews.is_empty()` → `EnvelopeShape` (L-CORE-30; ruling 2; Q18 "reply_to required non-null for 1–6"; DEV-W2-06). The body limit stays first, so a type-2 envelope with a body is `E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT` whether or not it names a target.
3. The `Attachment` doc comment says `blob_id` is the SHA-256 of the **stored bytes** (ciphertext ‖ tag) and that `thumb` is the **sealed** thumbnail (`crate::attachment::seal_thumb`), not decrypted media (DEV-W2-38); `Debug` prints `name` as `<n bytes>` and never its text (ruled: AI-6; the redaction rule of `:141-143`).
4. `crate::attachment` implements L-CORE-31 exactly: `seal_blob` = `Aes256Gcm::new(key.into()).encrypt(Nonce::from_slice(nonce), Payload { msg: plaintext, aad: AAD_BLOB })`, returning `ct ‖ tag`; `open_blob` checks in the order of its doc comment and compares `blob_id` with `!=` (a public hash; no constant-time need); `seal_thumb` refuses `plaintext.len() > MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT` with `ProtocolError::EnvelopeLimit` before sealing; `open_thumb` refuses `thumb.len() < TAG_LEN` and any AEAD failure with `ProtocolError::BlobOpen` (Q15; protocol/04 § Attachments as written in Step 4).
5. `ProtocolError::BlobOpen` ↔ `"E_BLOB_OPEN"` in `code()`, `from_code` and `Display`; it is not a hard reject (L-CORE-32).
6. `protocol/vectors/attachment.json` is written by the generator with WebCrypto (`crypto.subtle` AES-GCM, `tagLength: 128`, `additionalData` = the UTF-8 AAD; `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256')`), never by hand; its cases and rejects are exactly those of Step 5 (L-CORE-31; ruled: AI-1). The generator is deterministic: two runs write byte-identical files.
7. `protocol/vectors/envelope.json`: case 1's attachment gains `name: "wolf-capes.jpg"` and is regenerated; a fifth case "image message with a thumbnail and a name" (`msgId` 16×0x41, type 0, `threadId` null, `replyTo` null, body `""`, one attachment `blobId` 32×0x43, `key` 32×0x44, `nonce` 12×0x45, `size` 1234, `mime` `image/png`, `w` 640, `h` 480, `thumb` = `attachment.json` case 3's `thumb`, `name` `"map.png"`, previews `[]`, `kf` 32×0x46); `rejects` keeps its nine entries (their attachments now carry `name: "wolf-capes.jpg"`) and appends, in this order: "an edit with no reply_to" (`E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`), "a reaction carrying an attachment" (`E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`), "an attachment name one byte over 255" (`E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT`), "an attachment of eight elements" (`E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`) — 13 in all (L-CORE-30).
8. The Rust runner: `run_attachment()` (suite `"attachment"`, 14 fields: 3 + 3 + 5 + 3) and the six `attachment reject: <name>` rows plus the four new `envelope reject: <name>` rows in `run_rejects` (92 → 102); `run_all` returns seven suites in the order `envelope, franking, sframe, identity, frames, attachment, rejects` (ruled: AI-6); the report then holds 344 fields (15 + 4 + 176 + 8 + 25 + 14 + 102), all passing natively, on wasm32-unknown-unknown (`vectors_wasm.rs`, `node.rs`) and on wasm32-wasip1 through the Go golden (L-CORE-31).
9. The TS reference (`packages/protocol-vectors`): `encodeEnvelope`/`decodeEnvelope` use the 9-element attachment; `decodeEnvelope` throws `envelope: shape: …` for an attachment that is not a 9-element array and for the two type 1–6 rules, `envelope: limit exceeded: attachment name over 255 bytes` for the name; the generator's own test refuses every `envelope.json` reject with its code (`E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE` → `envelope: shape`) and every `attachment.json` reject with its code.
10. dillad's readable receiver (`ParseEnvelope`): `attachmentElements = 9`; `maxNameBytes = 255` checked with `mime` and `thumb` (`E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT`); a non-text `name` is `E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE` ("attachment %d: name must be a text string"); after `k_f` is decoded and before the mention count, a type other than 0 with `ReplyTo == nil` → `E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE` "type %d names its target in reply_to", and with attachments or previews → `E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE` "type %d carries no attachments or previews" (L-CORE-30). Every refusal is `400` with that code on `POST` and on `PATCH` (`readable.go:159, 372`).
11. **Attacker statement (lesson e), written beside the Rust and Go tests:** the new refusals reject only an envelope its own sender built wrongly; an honest client never sends a fold without a target or a fold carrying files, and no other member can make an honest member's envelope fail them (L-CORE-30). `open_blob`/`open_thumb` refuse only bytes that do not match what the sender sealed; the instance or anyone who swaps blob bytes gets `E_BLOB_HASH`, which is the check's purpose (protocol/04 § Attachments).

```rust
//! The attachment AEAD of protocol/04 § Attachments (Q15): AES-256-GCM under a random per-attachment
//! key and nonce, stored as ciphertext ‖ 16-byte tag, addressed by the SHA-256 of the stored bytes;
//! the thumbnail under the same key with the nonce's byte 11 XOR 0x01 and its own AAD.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::envelope::MAX_THUMB;
    use crate::error::ProtocolError;

    const KEY: [u8; 32] = [0x07; 32];
    const NONCE: [u8; 12] = [0x09; 12];

    #[test]
    fn the_constants_are_the_protocol_values() {
        assert_eq!(AAD_BLOB, b"dilla attachment v1");
        assert_eq!(AAD_THUMB, b"dilla thumb v1");
        assert_eq!(TAG_LEN, 16);
        assert_eq!(MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT, 8_176);
        assert_eq!(MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT + TAG_LEN, MAX_THUMB, "a sealed thumbnail fits the envelope bound");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_thumbnail_nonce_flips_the_low_bit_of_byte_eleven_only() {
        let mut want = [0u8; 12];
        want[11] = 0x01;
        assert_eq!(thumb_nonce(&[0u8; 12]), want);
        let n = [0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14, 0x15, 0x16, 0x17, 0x18, 0x19, 0x1a, 0x1b];
        let t = thumb_nonce(&n);
        assert_eq!(t[..11], n[..11]);
        assert_eq!(t[11], 0x1a);
        assert_eq!(thumb_nonce(&t), n);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_sealed_blob_is_ciphertext_and_tag_and_opens_to_the_plaintext() {
        let stored = seal_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, b"dilla");
        assert_eq!(stored.len(), 5 + TAG_LEN);
        assert_eq!(blob_id(&stored), crate::identity::sha256(&stored));
        assert_eq!(
            open_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, &blob_id(&stored), 5, &stored),
            Ok(b"dilla".to_vec())
        );
        let empty = seal_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, b"");
        assert_eq!(empty.len(), TAG_LEN, "an empty file is its tag");
        assert_eq!(open_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, &blob_id(&empty), 0, &empty), Ok(Vec::new()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_70000_byte_file_round_trips() {
        // (ruled: AI-1) the large-file coverage the vector file no longer carries.
        let plaintext: Vec<u8> = (0..70_000u32).map(|i| (i * 7 % 256) as u8).collect();
        let stored = seal_blob(&[0x57; 32], &[0x58; 12], &plaintext);
        assert_eq!(stored.len(), 70_016);
        assert_eq!(
            open_blob(&[0x57; 32], &[0x58; 12], &blob_id(&stored), 70_000, &stored),
            Ok(plaintext)
        );
    }

    /// Attacker statement (lesson e): `open_blob` refuses only bytes that are not what the sender
    /// sealed. Whoever swaps stored bytes (the instance, a proxy) meets the hash check first.
    #[test]
    fn open_blob_checks_the_hash_then_the_aead_then_the_size() {
        let stored = seal_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, b"dilla");
        let id = blob_id(&stored);
        let mut wrong_id = id;
        wrong_id[0] ^= 0x01;
        assert_eq!(open_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, &wrong_id, 5, &stored), Err(ProtocolError::BlobHash));
        let mut tampered = stored.clone();
        tampered[0] ^= 0x01;
        assert_eq!(
            open_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, &id, 5, &tampered),
            Err(ProtocolError::BlobHash),
            "the hash is checked before the AEAD"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            open_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, &blob_id(&tampered), 5, &tampered),
            Err(ProtocolError::BlobOpen)
        );
        assert_eq!(open_blob(&[0x08; 32], &NONCE, &id, 5, &stored), Err(ProtocolError::BlobOpen));
        assert_eq!(
            open_blob(&KEY, &thumb_nonce(&NONCE), &id, 5, &stored),
            Err(ProtocolError::BlobOpen)
        );
        assert_eq!(open_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, &id, 6, &stored), Err(ProtocolError::BlobOpen));
        let short = &stored[..TAG_LEN - 1];
        assert_eq!(
            open_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, &blob_id(short), 0, short),
            Err(ProtocolError::BlobOpen)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_two_aads_keep_a_file_and_a_thumbnail_apart() {
        let thumb = seal_thumb(&KEY, &NONCE, b"RIFF").expect("small");
        assert_eq!(
            open_blob(&KEY, &NONCE, &blob_id(&thumb), 4, &thumb),
            Err(ProtocolError::BlobOpen),
            "a thumbnail does not open as a file"
        );
        let blob = seal_blob(&KEY, &thumb_nonce(&NONCE), b"RIFF");
        assert_eq!(
            open_thumb(&KEY, &NONCE, &blob),
            Err(ProtocolError::BlobOpen),
            "a file sealed under the thumbnail nonce does not open as a thumbnail"
        );
        assert_eq!(open_thumb(&KEY, &NONCE, &thumb), Ok(b"RIFF".to_vec()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_thumbnail_is_bounded_so_its_sealed_form_fits_the_envelope() {
        let max = vec![0x5a; MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT];
        let sealed = seal_thumb(&KEY, &NONCE, &max).expect("at the bound");
        assert_eq!(sealed.len(), MAX_THUMB);
        assert_eq!(open_thumb(&KEY, &NONCE, &sealed), Ok(max));
        assert_eq!(
            seal_thumb(&KEY, &NONCE, &vec![0x5a; MAX_THUMB_PLAINTEXT + 1]),
            Err(ProtocolError::EnvelopeLimit)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            open_thumb(&KEY, &NONCE, &sealed[..TAG_LEN - 1]),
            Err(ProtocolError::BlobOpen)
        );
    }
}
```

  ```rust
      /// L-CORE-30: types 1..6 name their target and carry no files. Attacker statement: only the
      /// envelope's own sender can build one that fails; no member can make an honest envelope fail.
      #[test]
      fn types_one_to_six_require_reply_to_and_carry_no_attachments_or_previews() {
          for kind in [
              EnvelopeType::Edit,
              EnvelopeType::Delete,
              EnvelopeType::ReactionAdd,
              EnvelopeType::ReactionRemove,
              EnvelopeType::Pin,
              EnvelopeType::Unpin,
          ] {
              let mut env = base();
              env.kind = kind;
              env.body = match kind {
                  EnvelopeType::Edit => "fixed".to_owned(),
                  EnvelopeType::ReactionAdd | EnvelopeType::ReactionRemove => "👍".to_owned(),
                  _ => String::new(),
              };
              assert_eq!(env.validate(), Err(ProtocolError::EnvelopeShape), "{kind:?} without reply_to");
              env.reply_to = Some(MsgId::from_bytes([0x02; 16]));
              assert_eq!(env.validate(), Ok(()), "{kind:?} with reply_to");
              let bytes = env.encode().expect("encodes");
              assert_eq!(Envelope::decode(&bytes), Ok(env.clone()), "{kind:?} round trip");
              let mut with_file = env.clone();
              with_file.attachments = vec![sample_attachment()];
              assert_eq!(with_file.validate(), Err(ProtocolError::EnvelopeShape), "{kind:?} with a file");
              let mut with_preview = env.clone();
              with_preview.previews = vec![sample_preview()];
              assert_eq!(with_preview.validate(), Err(ProtocolError::EnvelopeShape), "{kind:?} with a preview");
          }
          let mut message = base();
          message.attachments = vec![sample_attachment()];
          assert_eq!(message.validate(), Ok(()), "a message stands alone and carries files");
          let mut tomb = base();
          tomb.kind = EnvelopeType::Delete;
          tomb.body = "x".to_owned();
          assert_eq!(tomb.validate(), Err(ProtocolError::EnvelopeLimit), "the body limit is checked first");
      }

      #[test]
      fn an_attachment_name_is_at_most_255_bytes() {
          assert_eq!(MAX_NAME, 255);
          let mut env = base();
          let mut a = sample_attachment();
          a.name = "n".repeat(MAX_NAME);
          env.attachments = vec![a.clone()];
          let bytes = env.encode().expect("at the bound");
          assert_eq!(Envelope::decode(&bytes).expect("decodes").attachments[0].name, "n".repeat(MAX_NAME));
          a.name = "n".repeat(MAX_NAME + 1);
          env.attachments = vec![a];
          assert_eq!(env.validate(), Err(ProtocolError::EnvelopeLimit));
          let mut e = Encoder::with_capacity(512);
          e.array(9).uint(1).bytes(&[0x01; 16]).uint(0).null().null().text("");
          e.array(1);
          e.array(9)
              .bytes(&[0x03; 32])
              .bytes(&[0x44; 32])
              .bytes(&[0x55; 12])
              .uint(1)
              .text("image/png")
              .null()
              .null()
              .null()
              .text(&"n".repeat(MAX_NAME + 1));
          e.array(0);
          e.bytes(&[0x06; 32]);
          assert_eq!(Envelope::decode(&e.into_vec()), Err(ProtocolError::EnvelopeLimit));
      }

      #[test]
      fn an_attachment_of_eight_elements_is_refused() {
          let mut e = Encoder::with_capacity(256);
          e.array(9).uint(1).bytes(&[0x01; 16]).uint(0).null().null().text("");
          e.array(1);
          e.array(8)
              .bytes(&[0x03; 32])
              .bytes(&[0x44; 32])
              .bytes(&[0x55; 12])
              .uint(1)
              .text("image/png")
              .null()
              .null()
              .null();
          e.array(0);
          e.bytes(&[0x06; 32]);
          assert_eq!(Envelope::decode(&e.into_vec()), Err(ProtocolError::EnvelopeShape));
  ```

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { AAD_BLOB, AAD_THUMB, AttachmentVectorError, attachmentVectors, openBlob, openThumb, sealBlob, sealThumb, thumbNonce } from './attachment.ts';
import { sha256 } from './hmac.ts';
import { fromHex, hex, utf8 } from './bytes.ts';
import { VECTORS_DIR } from './generate.ts';

type Case = { name: string; key: string; nonce: string; plaintext: string; size: number; stored: string; blob_id: string;
  thumb_nonce: string; thumb_plaintext: string | null; thumb: string | null };
type Reject = { name: string; kind: 'blob' | 'thumb'; key: string; nonce: string; blob_id?: string; size?: number; data: string; error: string };
const file = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(VECTORS_DIR, 'attachment.json'), 'utf8')) as {
  version: number; description: string; aad_blob: string; aad_thumb: string; cases: Case[]; rejects: Reject[];
};

async function codeOf(p: Promise<unknown>): Promise<string> {
  try { await p; return 'accepted'; } catch (e) { if (e instanceof AttachmentVectorError) return e.code; throw e; }
}

    expect(file.aad_blob).toBe(hex(utf8('dilla attachment v1')));
    expect(file.aad_thumb).toBe(hex(utf8('dilla thumb v1')));
    expect(hex(thumbNonce(fromHex('000102030405060708090a0b')))).toBe('000102030405060708090a0a');
  });

    expect(file.version).toBe(1);
    expect(file.cases.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(['empty file', 'one byte', 'a 1000-byte file with a thumbnail', 'a 300-byte file']);
    const [empty, one, thousand, last] = file.cases as [Case, Case, Case, Case];
    expect([empty.key, empty.nonce, empty.plaintext, empty.size]).toEqual(['51'.repeat(32), '52'.repeat(12), '', 0]);
    expect([one.key, one.nonce, one.plaintext, one.size]).toEqual(['53'.repeat(32), '54'.repeat(12), '2a', 1]);
    expect([thousand.key, thousand.nonce, thousand.size]).toEqual(['55'.repeat(32), '000102030405060708090a0b', 1000]);
    expect(thousand.plaintext).toBe(hex(Uint8Array.from({ length: 1000 }, (_, i) => i % 251)));
    expect(thousand.thumb_plaintext).toBe('52494646' + '12000000' + '57454250' + '00'.repeat(14));
    expect([last.key, last.nonce, last.size]).toEqual(['57'.repeat(32), '58'.repeat(12), 300]);
    expect(last.plaintext).toBe(hex(Uint8Array.from({ length: 300 }, (_, i) => (i * 7) % 256)));
    for (const c of [empty, one, last]) expect([c.thumb_plaintext, c.thumb], c.name).toEqual([null, null]);
  });

    for (const c of file.cases) {

      const stored = await sealBlob(key, nonce, plain);
      expect(hex(stored), c.name).toBe(c.stored);
      expect(stored.length, c.name).toBe(plain.length + 16);
      expect(hex(await sha256(stored)), c.name).toBe(c.blob_id);
      expect(hex(await openBlob(key, nonce, fromHex(c.blob_id), c.size, fromHex(c.stored))), c.name).toBe(c.plaintext);
      expect(c.thumb_nonce, c.name).toBe(hex(thumbNonce(nonce)));
      if (c.thumb_plaintext !== null && c.thumb !== null) {
        expect(hex(await sealThumb(key, nonce, fromHex(c.thumb_plaintext))), c.name).toBe(c.thumb);
        expect(hex(await openThumb(key, nonce, fromHex(c.thumb))), c.name).toBe(c.thumb_plaintext);
      }

      ['size disagrees', 'blob', 'E_BLOB_OPEN'],

      ['truncated below the tag', 'blob', 'E_BLOB_OPEN'],
    ]);

      const key = fromHex(r.key); const nonce = fromHex(r.nonce); const data = fromHex(r.data);
      const got = r.kind === 'blob'
        ? await codeOf(openBlob(key, nonce, fromHex(r.blob_id ?? ''), r.size ?? -1, data))
        : await codeOf(openThumb(key, nonce, data));
      expect(got, r.name).toBe(r.error);

});
```

```go
// protocol/04 requires of every receiver. Attacker statement: only the envelope's own sender can
// build one that fails, so the refusal is never something one member can do to another.
func TestFoldTypesNameATargetAndCarryNoFiles(t *testing.T) {
	att := api.Attachment{BlobID: make([]byte, 32), Key: make([]byte, 32), Nonce: make([]byte, 12), Size: 1, Mime: "image/png", Name: "map.png"}
	prev := api.Preview{URL: "https://x", Title: "t", Description: "d"}

		cases := []struct {
			name string
			b    []byte
			code string
		}{
			{"no reply_to", env9(typ, body, nil, nil), "E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE"},
			{"with a target", envWith(typ, body, seqRef(1), nil, nil), ""},
			{"with an attachment", envWith(typ, body, seqRef(1), []api.Attachment{att}, nil), "E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE"},
			{"with a preview", envWith(typ, body, seqRef(1), nil, []api.Preview{prev}), "E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE"},
		}
		for _, tc := range cases {
			t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("type %d %s", typ, tc.name), func(t *testing.T) {
				_, err := api.ParseEnvelope(tc.b)
				if tc.code == "" {
					if err != nil {
						t.Fatalf("ParseEnvelope: %v", err)
					}
					return
				}
				if got := codeOf(err); got != tc.code {
					t.Fatalf("code = %s (%v), want %s", got, err, tc.code)
				}
			})

	}
}
```

The server-readable paragraph (`:41-46`) moves, unchanged, to directly after the Limits paragraph. Then the attachment paragraph (`:31-34`) and the semantics paragraph (`:36-39`) are replaced by three new sections, placed before `## Deterministic CBOR`:
```
## Attachments

An attachment is a file the sender encrypts on its device and uploads as an opaque blob (`09` §
Blobs). The envelope carries everything a receiver needs to fetch and open it; the instance learns
the blob's size and the channel it was stored for, nothing else.

- **Key and nonce.** The sender draws `key` (32 bytes) and `nonce` (12 bytes) at random for every
  attachment and never uses them for anything else.
- **The file.** `stored = AES-256-GCM(key, nonce, aad = "dilla attachment v1", plaintext = the
  file)`, written as the ciphertext followed by the 16-byte tag and nothing else: the nonce travels
  only in the envelope. `size` is the plaintext's length in bytes; `blob_id = SHA-256(stored)`.
- **The thumbnail.** Optional, for an image. Its plaintext is a WebP image (a JPEG where the
  sender's platform cannot encode WebP) whose longest side is at most 320 px and whose length is at
  most 8 176 bytes; `thumb = AES-256-GCM(key, thumb_nonce, aad = "dilla thumb v1", plaintext)`, where
  `thumb_nonce` is `nonce` with its byte 11 XORed with 0x01, so the sealed thumbnail is at most
  8 192 bytes.
- **The name.** `name` is the file's name as the sender gives it (UTF-8, `""` when none). It is
  never a path: a receiver removes control and bidirectional-control characters and path separators
  before it shows or saves a name, and refuses an envelope for a name's length only.
- **Receiving.** A receiver that downloads a blob checks, in this order: `SHA-256(stored) =
  blob_id`, else it refuses the file with `E_BLOB_HASH`; `stored` is at least 16 bytes, opens under
  `key`, `nonce` and `"dilla attachment v1"`, and the plaintext is `size` bytes long, else
  `E_BLOB_OPEN`. A thumbnail that does not open under `key`, `thumb_nonce` and `"dilla thumb v1"` is
  `E_BLOB_OPEN`. A refused attachment is not shown; the rest of the envelope is.
- **Rendering.** `mime` is the sender's claim. A receiver renders a file as an image only when its
  `mime` is `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp` or `image/gif`, and a thumbnail only when its
  plaintext begins with `RIFF` and holds `WEBP` at offset 8, or begins with the bytes `FF D8 FF`;
  everything else is a file to save.
- **References.** The sender's client deletes its blob references when it discards a message
  before sending it and when it deletes a message (§ Semantics).

Previews are generated by the **sender**; receivers MUST NOT fetch remote resources for an
envelope.

## Semantics

Types 1 to 6 **fold** onto a target: the message whose `msg_id` their `reply_to` names, in the same
group. A receiver applies the rules below to the rows it holds, ordered by the group's `seq`, and
recomputes them whenever a row they depend on arrives or is deleted, so the outcome does not depend
on the order in which rows reach it.

- **Target.** The target of `X` in a group is the earliest (lowest `seq`) type-0 envelope with
  `msg_id = X` the receiver holds there, shown or deleted. A later type-0 envelope that repeats `X`
  is shown as its own message and is never a target. A fold whose target is not held is kept, not
  shown, and applied when the target arrives.
- **Delete wins.** A type-2 envelope from the target's author (the same `user_id` in the MLS
  credential, from any of the author's devices), or the delivery service's deletion of the target
  (`02` message delete, gateway `message.deleted`), deletes the target: its body, attachments and
  previews are no longer shown, the bodies of its edits are dropped, and its reactions and its pin
  are removed. It applies whichever of the two arrives first. It applies also when the target
  itself is not held: a receiver then drops the bodies of the type-1 envelopes from the same author
  that name the target. A type-2 envelope from anyone else changes nothing. The sender's client also
  asks the delivery service to delete its copy, which the service does only for the uploading user
  (`02`), and deletes the message's blob references.
- **Edit.** Of the type-1 envelopes from the target's author, the one with the highest `seq`
  replaces the shown body. An edit from anyone else changes nothing. An edit raises no mention.
- **Reactions.** A reaction is kept per user and emoji: of the type-3 and type-4 envelopes from one
  user with one `body` on a target, the one with the highest `seq` decides whether that user's
  reaction is present (3) or not (4). A user adds and removes only their own reactions.
- **Pins.** Of the type-5 and type-6 envelopes on a target, the one with the highest `seq` decides
  whether it is pinned (5) or not (6), from any member. This version checks no role snapshot: the
  former rule that a pin needs the channel's pin permission in the receiver's role snapshot is not
  applied, and a client shows who pinned.
- A fold that breaks a rule is ignored, never an error; only § Envelope refuses an envelope.

## Mentions

The body of a type-0 or type-1 envelope may mention someone with the readable syntax of `09` §
Readable channels: `<@` followed by the 32 lower-case hexadecimal digits of a user id or a role id
and `>`, `<@everyone>`, or `<@here>`. A receiver matches the tokens literally (lower-case hex only;
no other spelling is a mention) and counts a type-0 message as mentioning it when the message comes
from another user and carries the receiver's own user id, a role id the receiver holds in that
community, `<@everyone>` or `<@here>`. This version gates neither `<@everyone>` nor `<@here>` on the
`mention_everyone` permission and counts `<@here>` as `<@everyone>`. An edit never raises a mention.
A client shows a mention as the name it stands for, never as the raw token.
```

```
`vectors/attachment.json` carries a `rejects` array too: six stored blobs or thumbnails a receiver
must refuse, each with its code — a `blob_id` that does not match (`E_BLOB_HASH`); a flipped tag
bit, a file sealed under the thumbnail AAD, a `size` that disagrees, a thumbnail sealed under the
file's own nonce and stored bytes shorter than the tag (`E_BLOB_OPEN`).
```

**Requirements:**
1. **Schema v3** (L-SQL-30; Q23; lesson g). `APP_SCHEMA` creates `app_messages` with `reply_to BLOB`, `edit_body TEXT`, `edit_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` inline after `mention`, creates the four new tables, and seeds `('schema', x'03')`; it names no v3 column in an index. A fresh v3 store and a store migrated from v1 or v2 have identical `pragma_table_info` for every app table and identical app index lists.
2. `migrate_conn`: `APP_SCHEMA`; read `schema` (a value that is not one CBOR uint → `StorageError::Codec("app_meta schema is malformed")`, web-1 text); found 1 → `MIGRATE_V1_TO_V2` then `MIGRATE_V2_TO_V3`; found 2 → `MIGRATE_V2_TO_V3`; then when found ≤ 3, `APP_INDEXES_V3`; return found. `migrate_app` and `open` run, in the one unit: found 1 → `backfill` (web-2a, unchanged) then `backfill_v3`; found 2 → `backfill_v3`. A failure anywhere rolls back every DDL statement (SQLite DDL is transactional), so the store stays at the schema it had. `open` refuses found > 3 with `E_CORE_STATE` "app schema <n> is newer than this build".
3. `backfill_v3(u)`: (a) for every row `status = 0 AND envelope IS NOT NULL`, set `reply_to` to element 4 of the stored envelope read structurally (a nine-element CBOR array; element 4 a 16-byte bstr or null; nothing else validated). Bytes that are not such an array → `StorageError::Codec("app_messages envelope does not decode")`, rolling the migration back (ruled: AI-2). (b) For every distinct `(group_id, reply_to)` of a row with `status = 0 AND type BETWEEN 1 AND 6 AND reply_to IS NOT NULL`, `refold(c, group_id, reply_to, &FoldScope::Full, None, None)`. `mention` flags stay as v2 set them; no purge, no role is written.
4. **The fold** (L-CORE-33 steps 1–5, exactly as the ledger, every read of `app_messages` restricted to `status = 0` unless stated): target resolution = `SELECT seq, status, sender_user, COALESCE(edit_body, body) FROM app_messages WHERE group_id = ?1 AND msg_id = ?2 AND type = 0 AND status IN (0, 2) ORDER BY seq LIMIT 1`; no target → for `Full` and `Edit` only, for every distinct `sender_user` `U` of a status-0 type-2 row with `reply_to = target`, every status-0 type-1 row with `reply_to = target` and `sender_user = U` gets `body = '', envelope = NULL` (FACTS-SECURITY-03: only a user's own delete blanks only that user's edits), and nothing else is written. Delete wins (target status 2, or a status-0 type-2 row with `reply_to = target` and `sender_user = T.sender_user`): the target becomes `status = 2, body = '', envelope = NULL, reason = '', edit_body = NULL, edit_seq = 0`; every type-1 row with `reply_to = target` gets `body = '', envelope = NULL`; the target's `app_reactions` and `app_pins` rows are deleted; stop. Edit: the highest-`seq` type-1 row from `T.sender_user` → `edit_body, edit_seq` (none → `NULL, 0`). Reactions: per `(sender_user, body)` among types 3 and 4 the highest `seq` decides (3 present, 4 absent). Pins: the highest-`seq` type 5 or 6 decides (5 → upsert `seq`, `by_user`; 6 or none → delete). Nothing refuses; `refold` is idempotent. Every statement over `app_messages` by `reply_to` is a `pub(super) const` of `fold.rs` and an index search on one of the three fold indexes (Requirement 12).
5. `refold` is called in the same unit as the write that causes it (L-CORE-33): after every status-0 insert of type 1–6 (target = its `reply_to`, scope = `fold::scope_of` of the inserted row, a trigger) and of type 0 (target = its `msg_id`, scope `Full`, a trigger) — the received insert in `group_apply`, the own adoption in `apply_message`, `send_confirm`'s insert; after the own deleted marker (target by its type, scope = `fold::scope_of` of the marker's envelope, no trigger); after `message_deleted` and rule 2 turn a stored row to status 2 (target = the row's `msg_id` when it was type 0, its `reply_to` when it was type 1–6, nothing when its type is NULL; scope = `fold::scope_of` of the row's `type`, `sender_user` and `body` read before the UPDATE; no trigger). The backfill passes `FoldScope::Full`. Every inserted row stores `reply_to` = its envelope's (the own deleted marker included). The result shapes of `group_apply`, `message_deleted`, `send_confirm` do not change (`group_apply_parity.json` stays at 8 cases).
6. **The timeline view** (L-CORE-34; ruling 9): `own()` first (`E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY`), then the web-1 checks (`limit` 1..=200 → else `E_CORE_INPUT` "limit out of range"; unknown group `E_CORE_NOT_FOUND`); the page is `seq DESC LIMIT limit` over displayable rows only, answered ascending. Body: status 0 → `COALESCE(edit_body, body)`, else `""`. Reply: present only for a status-0 row whose `reply_to` is not NULL; state 0 (target status 0, excerpt of its shown body), 1 (no target: `target_seq`, `target_user` null, excerpt `""`), 2 (target status 2: its seq and user, excerpt `""`). Excerpt: the first 120 Unicode scalar values of the shown body with every `\n` and `\r` replaced by a space. Reactions and pinned: only for a status-0 type-0 row that is its msg id's target (no earlier status-0-or-2 type-0 row with the msg id; ruled: AI-4); reactions grouped by emoji, `count` = rows, `mine` = 1 when a row's `user_id` is the own user, ordered by `MIN(seq)` then emoji. Attachments: only for a status-0 type-0 row, from its stored envelope (`[]` when `Envelope::decode` refuses it; ruled: AI-2), `index` its position. `mention` = the stored flag. Reactions: at most 20 emoji — the 20 with the highest count, ties by the lower first seq then emoji — emitted ordered by first seq then emoji (ruling 32).
7. **Pins** (L-CORE-35): `own()` first; unknown group → `E_CORE_NOT_FOUND`; every `app_pins` row of the group, `seq DESC`, whose target resolves → `[T.seq, target, pin seq, by_user, T.sender_user, excerpt(T's shown body), T.recv_ts]`. Each row ends with the target's `recv_ts` (seven elements; ruling 36).
8. **Own roles and role mentions** (L-CORE-35; Q20; ruling 12): `own_roles_set` — `own()` first; `role_ids.len()` not a multiple of 16 or over 1024 → `E_CORE_INPUT` "role_ids must be 0..=64 ids of 16 bytes"; then in one unit `DELETE FROM app_roles WHERE community_id = ?1` and `INSERT OR IGNORE` each id. No row is re-flagged. `mentions_me_with_roles(body, user, roles)` = `mentions_me(body, user)` or the body contains `"<@" + 32 lower-case hex of a role + ">"`. `group_apply`'s received insert sets `mention` on a status-0 type-0 row from another user with `mentions_me_with_roles(body, own.user_id, <the role ids of app_roles joined to the group's community_id>)`; a DM (null community) has none. An edit never raises a mention (ruling 4).
9. **Attacker statements (lesson e), beside the tests:** an edit or a delete from anyone but the target's author changes nothing (steps 2–3 compare `sender_user`, which the MLS credential authenticates, `sync.rs:606`); a member cannot remove or forge another member's reaction (step 4 is keyed by the authenticated sender); a pin or unpin from any member is accepted (Q20's recorded deviation; `pins` names who pinned); a fold aimed at a msg id the device does not hold costs only the row it stores anyway; a replayed type-0 row never becomes a target. Nothing here refuses. The migration's only new refusal (`E_CORE_STORAGE` "app_messages envelope does not decode", `E_CORE_STATE` for schema > 3) is reached only by a store this build's cores did not write: every stored envelope was a nine-element array when stored (ruled: AI-2). Any member could have sent a web-2a browser a type 1–6 envelope without `reply_to` or an eight-element attachment; the structural walk accepts both, so no message another member sent can keep a store from opening (FACTS-SECURITY-01). An author's type 2 naming a target the device never held blanks only that author's own type-1 rows (FACTS-SECURITY-03); the reaction cap (20 chips) bounds what any member's distinct emoji can add to the view and hides only the least-counted chips (FACTS-SECURITY-02).
10. **TypeScript** (L-TS-30; ruling 19): `TimelineRow` and its three nested types as the Interfaces; `readTimeline` decodes `arr(v, 18)` and each nested value with its exact count (`arr(…, 5)` reply, `arr(…, 3)` reaction, `arr(…, 7)` attachment), the flags with `oneOf(…, [0, 1])`, `state` with `oneOf(…, [0, 1, 2])`, sizes and indexes with `u53`; a wrong shape is `E_CORE_DECODE` as every decoder. `ModelCore.timeline` answers displayable rows only with `editedSeq: 0n, reply: null, reactions: [], pinned: false, attachments: []` and `mention` = the core's flag rule (status 0, type 0, another user, `mentionsMe(body)`).
11. The wasm budget for this task is 49,152 B over the size recorded in Step 0.
12. **Scoped refolds** (L-CORE-33; FACTS-SECURITY-02): `refold` runs steps 1 and 2 for every scope; step 3 for `Full` and `Edit`; step 4 for `Full` (every `(user, emoji)` pair) and `Reaction` (that pair only); step 5 for `Full` and `Pin`; step 1's unheld branch for `Full` and `Edit`. Results are identical to a full recompute; the scope only bounds the work (L-CORE-33; ruling 32). Every statement `refold` runs against `app_messages` by `reply_to` is one of the eight `pub(super) const`s of `fold.rs` (Step 6), and each one's `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` names one of `app_messages_by_reply`, `app_messages_by_pin`, `app_messages_by_reaction` and never `SCAN app_messages` (`fold::tests::every_fold_statement_is_an_index_search`).

```rust
/// A type-`kind` envelope as the fold tests send it (web-2b task 2): no thread, files or previews,
/// `k_f` 32 × 0x06.
pub fn fold_envelope(
    msg_id: [u8; 16],
    kind: EnvelopeType,
    reply_to: Option<[u8; 16]>,
    body: &str,
) -> Envelope {
    Envelope {
        v: 1,
        msg_id: MsgId::from_bytes(msg_id),
        kind,
        thread_id: None,
        reply_to: reply_to.map(MsgId::from_bytes),
        body: body.to_owned(),
        attachments: Vec::new(),
        previews: Vec::new(),
        k_f: [0x06; 32],
    }
}
```
and in `impl RawPeer` replace `send_typed` (`:1181-1206`) by:
```rust
    pub fn send_typed(&mut self, relay: &mut Relay, kind: EnvelopeType, body: &str) -> u64 {
        let reply_to = (kind != EnvelopeType::Message).then_some([0x5b; 16]);
        self.send_envelope(relay, &fold_envelope([0x5a; 16], kind, reply_to, body))
    }

    /// Uploads `envelope` as one application message; answers its seq.
    pub fn send_envelope(&mut self, relay: &mut Relay, envelope: &Envelope) -> u64 {
        let group = self.group.as_mut().expect("created");
        let blob = group
            .create_message(&self.provider, &self.signer, envelope)
            .expect("create_message")
            .tls_serialize_detached()
            .expect("serialize");
        let mut e = Encoder::new();
        e.array(2).uint(group.epoch()).bytes(&blob);
        let answer = relay
            .post_message(self.device, &e.into_vec())
            .expect("upload");
        seq_of_answer(&answer)
    }

    /// Processes and merges another member's commit, the relay's handshake row at `seq`.
    pub fn apply_commit(&mut self, relay: &Relay, seq: u64) {
        let row = relay
            .handshakes
            .iter()
            .find(|h| h.seq == seq)
            .expect("a handshake row at that seq");
        let message = protocol_in(&row.blob).expect("a protocol message");
        let group = self.group.as_mut().expect("joined");
        match group
            .process_message(&self.provider, message)
            .expect("process the commit")
        {
            DillaProcessed::StagedCommit(staged) => group
                .merge_staged_commit(&self.provider, *staged)
                .expect("merge"),
            other => panic!("expected a commit at seq {seq}, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }
```

```rust
/// A private copy of the committed fixture `src` under the temp directory, opened as a file.
fn copy_of(src: &str, name: &str) -> (PathBuf, ConnHandle) {
    let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
        "dilla-client-migrate-{}-{name}.db",
        std::process::id()
    ));
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);
    std::fs::copy(src, &path).expect("copy the fixture");
    let conn: ConnHandle = Arc::new(Mutex::new(
        rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).expect("open the copy"),
    ));
    (path, conn)
}

fn fixture_copy(name: &str) -> (PathBuf, ConnHandle) {
    copy_of(FIXTURE, name)
}

fn app_indexes(c: &rusqlite::Connection) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut stmt = c
        .prepare("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'index' AND name LIKE 'app%' ORDER BY name")
        .expect("prepare");
    stmt.query_map([], |r| r.get::<_, String>(0))
        .expect("query")
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
        .expect("names")
}
```

```rust
const V2_FIXTURE: &str = concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/tests/fixtures/app_v2.db");

/// web-2a's `APP_SCHEMA` (L-SQL-20), verbatim (`src/client/schema.rs:67-128` at `89ea4e0`).
const APP_SCHEMA_V2: &str = "
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_meta (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_groups (
  group_id     BLOB    PRIMARY KEY CHECK (length(group_id) = 16),
  kind         INTEGER NOT NULL,
  community_id BLOB    CHECK (community_id IS NULL OR length(community_id) = 16),
  target_id    BLOB    NOT NULL CHECK (length(target_id) = 16),
  state        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  next_seq     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  acked_seq    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  acked_epoch  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  resync       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (resync IN (0, 1)),
  was_gone     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (was_gone IN (0, 1)),
  max_epoch    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  epoch          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  pending_commit INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS app_groups_by_target ON app_groups (target_id, kind) WHERE state <> 4;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_handshake_tail (
  group_id BLOB NOT NULL, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, epoch INTEGER NOT NULL, kind INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sender INTEGER, blob BLOB NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (group_id, seq)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_proposals (
  group_id BLOB NOT NULL, ref BLOB NOT NULL, epoch INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (group_id, ref)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_messages (
  group_id      BLOB    NOT NULL,
  seq           INTEGER NOT NULL,
  epoch         INTEGER NOT NULL,
  recv_ts       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  status        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason        TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  sender_user   BLOB,
  sender_device BLOB    NOT NULL,
  sender_leaf   INTEGER,
  sender_kind   INTEGER,
  sender_tier   INTEGER,
  msg_id        BLOB,
  type          INTEGER,
  body          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  envelope      BLOB,
  franking_tag  BLOB    NOT NULL,
  mention       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (group_id, seq)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS app_messages_by_msg ON app_messages (group_id, msg_id);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_outbox (
  msg_id   BLOB    PRIMARY KEY CHECK (length(msg_id) = 16),
  group_id BLOB    NOT NULL,
  envelope BLOB    NOT NULL,
  created  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  state    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  error    TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  epoch    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS app_outbox_by_group ON app_outbox (group_id, created, msg_id);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_read_state (
  group_id      BLOB    PRIMARY KEY CHECK (length(group_id) = 16),
  last_read_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_read_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_settings (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO app_meta (k, v) VALUES ('schema', x'02');
";
```
